LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Here's how to watch, what to know, and an expert prediction before the Pats and Bears face off in Chicago Getty Images In the Week 7 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Chicago Bears play host to the New England Patriots . Chicago is coming off a win in Caleb Williams ' return to the lineup, having held on for a 31-23 victory in a game that moved the Bears to 4-2 on the season. The Bears bounced back from their dispiriting loss to the division rival Green Bay Packers the week before, when the offense looked like a disaster with backup Tyson Bagent under center. Chicago will look to keep the good times rolling here. New England also won what -- on the surface -- looked like a close game against the New York Jets , but finished with a seven-point margin of victory thanks only to a late field goal. The Patriots have won three consecutive games after starting the season 1-2, and their quarterback has found a groove after looking nearly broken to start the year. The Pats, too, are looking to keep the train on the tracks on Thursday night. Will the Bears capture another win, or will the Patriots continue their hot streak? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Bears vs. Patriots live Date: Thursday, Oct. 22 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Soldier Field (Chicago) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bears -3, O/U 50.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Patriots have the ball Drake Maye has found himself over the last three weeks, completing 66 of 103 passes for 878 yards, 10 touchdowns, and one interception after going just 51-of-80 for 585 yards, one touchdown, and six picks through the first three games of the season. Maye has rediscovered the deep ball, in particular, going 12 of 20 for 350 yards and four scores on throws beyond 15 yards in the last three games, per Tru Media. Before that, he was just 9 of 20 for 281 yards and four interceptions on those throws. Maye finished with a strong game against the Jets despite A.J. Brown looking horrifyingly bad in his return from an ankle injury. Brown dropped (at least) three passes and turned his 10 targets into only 27 yards. Maye also lost Romeo Doubs to a shoulder injury on an early-game touchdown pass, so he was working with a limited receiving corps behind Brown. Still, he threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns without turning the ball over. Brown will presumably be better here, and Chicago hasn't been great against outside receivers, but last week's return of Kyler Gordon could lead to slot man Demario Douglas having a tougher go of things than he has over the last few weeks. Kyle Williams could get in on the action with Doubs sidelined, though Efton Chism has been getting more snaps because the Patriots trust him as a blocker. Chicago checks in a surprising eighth in opponents' EPA per dropback so far this season, per Tru Media, thanks to a high sack rate and a few timely interceptions. Opponents have averaged 8.4 yards per attempt against the Bears, though, indicating that you can indeed move the ball through the air if you can get a pass off and avoid a turnover. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has generated pressure at an above-average rate (39.7% of dropbacks) despite working with a somewhat limited group up front, and the Patriots will be without two starting guards here. So, the running backs (particularly Rhamondre Stevenson ) will have to be on their game in pass protection on Thursday night. The Patriots have struggled to run the ball thus far this season, with Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner combining for an average of just 3.9 yards per carry on 151 rushing attempts. Stevenson leads the way in the backfield largely because the Patriots trust him the most in short yardage and pass protection, but he hasn't been efficient or explosive. Henderson had an explosive rushing touchdown on his first run of the season but has failed to record one since. Kiner was a little-used third-stringer until he salted away the game against the Jets last Sunday. He could perhaps work his way into more touches after a nice showing in that game, given the rushing struggles of the two leads and the fact that Henderson also fumbled against New York. The Bears have allowed opponents 4.4 yards per carry on running-back rushes so far this season, with much of the success coming by way of yards before contact. It may be difficult for the Patriots to generate those types of yards with their injury issues along the offensive line, and their backs haven't exactly done the best job of breaking tackles this year, so the challenge of moving the offense down the field will likely fall squarely on Maye's right shoulder. When the Bears have the ball Caleb Williams returned last week from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury and looked no worse for wear. Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. The Bears kept things simple for him with a 3.9-yard average depth of throw (eighth-lowest for any quarterback in a single game this season), per Tru Media, and he was extremely efficient as a result. Williams has only played in three games so far this year, but he's leading the league with a 72.5% completion rate and is up to a career-best 7.8 yards per attempt. And that's despite a truly awful game against the Vikings in Week 2, where he went 15-of-26 for just 138 yards and an interception. In his first couple of appearances, it seemed like journeyman wideout Kalif Raymond (14 targets in Weeks 1 and 2) was his primary option, but on Sunday, it was Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland -- the most expected options -- leading the way with eight and seven targets, respectively. Rome Odunze saw five looks. Given the way they're each deployed, it seems likely that Odunze will see a bunch of Christian Gonzalez 's coverage on Thursday night -- especially with Carlton Davis III ruled out. Odunze is the biggest of the trio and plays most often on the perimeter, and he also tends to run the most routes. If that's the way things go, we should expect the passing game to flow through Burden and Loveland yet again. The Patriots have allowed opponents to complete 31 of 46 passes for 301 yards on throws to the slot this season, per Tru Media. Burden could have a nice night working inside if he's on the field more often than he was last week (eight targets on only 18 routes), though Marcus Jones does have an interception this season and is allowing only 1.46 yards per coverage snap in the slot, per Pro Football Focus. By contrast, New England has allowed only 29 catches for 279 yards to tight ends to date, so Loveland may not find the coverage as friendly. The Bears would do well to line him up all over the formation rather than solely in line, and perhaps use multi-tight end sets where he plays more of a receiver role, and Cole Kmet or Sam Roush handles the blocking aspects of the position. The Bears also tried against Atlanta to do what they do best: run the ball with volume. D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson (the latter filling in for the injured Kyle Monangai ) combined for 29 carries. They ran for only 96 yards on those totes, but they did find the end zone three times. Chicago's offensive line actually created some nice push, generating 1.45 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, but the backs slumped to only 1.83 yards after contact, as they combined for only four broken tackles. (For context, consider that the Seahawks ' running backs combined for 10 in their awful game against the Broncos on Thursday night.) The Pats have allowed only 3.9 yards per rush this season, thanks in part to yielding an average of only 0.75 yards before contact. Swift and Johnson (Monangai is out again) will have to do a better job of breaking tackles this time around if they want to generate yardage and create favorable down-and-distance scenarios for Williams and the passing game. I see this being a high-scoring game, what with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27 Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. Maybe Green Bay can actually run with some efficiency in Josh Jacobs ' potential return, but it's not like he was all that efficient last season, either. away.blurb: Doubs landed hard on his right shoulder, and after getting tended to by the training staff on the field, he eventually made his way to the sideline. He was initially listed as questionable to return but he was ruled out early in the second half. Doubs has 14 receptions for 261 yards and 3 touchdowns this season. Sunday marked the return of A.J. Brown, which was supposed to slot the receivers into their proper spot on the depth chart. But Doubs' injury threatens that scenario moving forward. It wasn't immediately clear what happened to Moses, as he went down after a non-contact injury. The team announced that it was an ankle injury. Like Doubs, Moses was initially listed as questionable to return but was later ruled out. The 35-year-old Moses took over 94 percent of the Patriots' offensive snaps last year and just under 93 percent this year. He was replaced Sunday by rookie Caleb Lomu, who was available because Will Campbell -- who suffered a knee sprain last week -- was able to play at left tackle. Vera-Tucker entered this game having played 100 percent of the Patriots' offensive snaps, but he wasn't able to return to the game. With Vera-Tucker out, Ben Brown -- who's in for the injured Mike Onwenu at right guard -- moved over to left guard, while Matt Pryor came in at right guard. The Patriots signed Pryor off the Cardinals' practice squad two weeks ago. Brown was ruled out shortly after he slowly made his way to the sideline. His departure brought Walter Rouse -- the Patriots' final healthy lineman -- into the game at guard. Jones, though, was able to shake it off and return to the field, which puts this one officially in the "injury scare" bucket. On Wednesday, the Patriots ruled out LG Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring), RG Ben Brown (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (neck), CB Karon Prunty (hamstring), and CB Channing Canada (hamstring). The Patriots are also listing RT Morgan Moses (foot), S Kevin Byard III (chest), S Craig Woodson (shoulder), and LB Christian Ellliss (chest) as questionable for Thursday night's game. Starting on offense, the Patriots offensive line will be shorthanded, with the Pats down multiple guards who have started games this season. Along with starting RG Mike Onwenu (ankle) and top backup Greg Van Roten (thigh), who are on injured reserve, New England is also down Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and Brown (knee). In his final press conference before Thursday night's game, head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed that Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor will start vs. the Bears. If Moses can't finish the game and the Patriots start Lomu at guard, the rookie would need to kick back outside. Vrabel also hinted at Lomu being prepared to be the backup center. In short, that's a lot of moving parts to plan for in-game contingencies, so the clearest path forward is to start Rouse and Pryor at guard while Lomu continues in his role as the top swing tackle. Plus, Moses is listed as questionable, and if he doesn't play on the short week, Lomu would make his first NFL start at right tackle. New England's available wideouts are Brown, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism III, while OC Josh McDaniels can use all his tight ends and running backs. Pittsburgh is 4-2 after a 26-19 overtime win over Tampa Bay, while New Orleans is 2-4 after beating the Giants 34-27. Kickoff is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET. With both teams coming off big wins in Week 6, let's take a look at the matchup and the bold predictions for Week 7 in Paris, France. Chris Boswell kicks five field goals, two from 50-plus © Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images Boswell is 13-for-17 on field goals this season, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards. Against Tampa Bay he went 4-for-5, with makes from 52 and 58 yards. That was his second straight game with multiple field goals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) New Orleans allows 29.7 points and 377.7 yards per game. Those numbers suggest Pittsburgh will move the ball. Some of those drives will stall before the end zone, and that is where Boswell scores. The prediction goes beyond another solid outing. Boswell makes five field goals, including two from beyond 50 yards. The limitation is his four misses this season, which show he is not automatic from long range. Tyler Shough throws two interceptions Shough has a 12:5 touchdown-to-interception ratio through six games. He threw only 144 yards against the Giants, though he scored four touchdowns in total. He is also playing through broken bones in his non-throwing hand, which may explain why he has just 242 passing yards over the last two weeks. Predicting two interceptions means Shough nearly matches his early-season total in one afternoon. The route to that outcome is straightforward. Pittsburgh's lead will push New Orleans into longer passing situations, and an injured hand makes tight-window throws harder. The call is that one pass is tipped and picked off in the second half, while another is forced into coverage on a late drive. Those turnovers would turn a competitive game into a Steelers cushion. There is a counterpoint. Shough has produced touchdowns despite modest yardage, so this prediction depends on game script more than on his recent efficiency. Chris Olave posts 120 yards and two touchdowns in a losing rally Olave had double-digit targets in each of the first four games. Over the last two he has seen only 13 targets, producing an 8-89-1 line. That drop in volume looks like the sort of dip that corrects itself. Pittsburgh's defense will give him room to correct it. New Orleans' opponents have averaged 256.0 passing yards per game, which suggests quarterbacks can find openings in this matchup. Rookie Germie Bernard's 11-catch, 87-yard, one-touchdown game against the Steelers' last opponent shows how that kind of volume can arise. Olave reaches 10 targets, 120 yards and two touchdowns as New Orleans chases points. Those scores help the Saints cut a two-score deficit to three points late in the fourth quarter. Pittsburgh still holds on. The prediction is Steelers 31, Saints 27, with Boswell's late field goal sealing it. If Jordyn Tyson makes his debut after traveling with the team while recovering from a hamstring injury, the Saints' receiving group could be even more dangerous. These are deliberately high-variance predictions, not the most likely outcomes. The underlying numbers favor Pittsburgh, but turnovers and a motivated passing offense can make this matchup less predictable than the records suggest. picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Saints Week 7 Tracker: Injury updates, predictions, storylines and more - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview Pittsburgh Steelers WR DK Metcalf (L) and New Orleans Saints RB Alvin Kamara | Brian Fluharty - Imagn Images and Michael Owens - Getty Images | Graphic by Adam Patrick Shayne Kubas Wed, October 21, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers will make NFL history this week, as will their opponent, the New Orleans Saints. For the first time in the league's long existence, a regular season game will be played in France. Paris, to be exact. After nearly 20 years since the Dolphins and Giants played the first regular season game outside of North America, the NFL's international footprint grows larger every year. As interesting as all of that is, the football played on the field is what really matters. Pittsburgh enters Week 7 with a 4-2 record, barely beating the Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime a week ago. The Saints, meanwhile, climbed to 2-4 after a bizarre 34-27 win over the Giants. Both teams have plenty of flaws they are hoping to correct as the season goes on, but the Steelers are favored for a reason. As the game approaches, we will have all of the important details you need to know. Injury reports, weather reports, how to watch, storylines, and more. So bookmark this page and come back throughout the week! How to Watch Pittsburgh Steelers vs New Orleans Saints in Week 7 Date: Sunday, October 25 Time: 9:30 a.m. EST TV Network: NFL Network Announcers: Dave Pasch (Play-by-Play), Kurt Warner and Jason Kelce (Color Analysts), Molly McGrath (Sideline Reporter) Pittsburgh Steelers Injury Report for Week 7 Steelers injury reports will appear here as they become available New Orleans Saints Injury Report for Week 7 Saints injury reports will appear here as they become available Weather Forecast for Pittsburgh Steelers vs New Orleans Saints Week 7 Current Forecast ( via NFLWeather.com ) Temperature: TBD Wind Speed: TBD Precipitation: TBD Biggest Pittsburgh Steelers Storylines heading into Week 7 Will the Steelers continue leaning on the passing game despite missing multiple playmakers? Despite missing multiple receivers heading into their Week 6 matchup with the Buccaneers, the Steelers chose to make the passing game the focal point of the offense. While they ultimately came away with the victory, it was an ugly mess for much of the contest. Aaron Rodgers put up a solid 253 yards through the air, but it took him a whopping 49 pass attempts to get there. He was the definition of a checkdown merchant , with just five of those 49 passes traveling beyond 10 yards, according to Next Gen Stats . It seemed as though Mike McCarthy didn't have faith that Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle could succeed against the Buccaneers' stout run defense. Still, the Steelers can't win games against good teams with that offensive approach. The Saints could be a team that they can once again get away with it against, but it's something to monitor. Which team will handle the international trip better? There has been plenty of discourse surrounding how to handle playing across the pond ever since the NFL's International Series took shape. We saw the Rams be criticized for arriving in Australia right before their Week 1 disaster against the 49ers, who had been down under for days at that point. In the Steelers case, they are taking the route of trying to make the week feel as normal as possible, choosing to fly out on Thursday evening. Meanwhile, the Saints arrived in France on Monday, so they will be well adjusted by game time on Sunday. Will the contrasting strategies make any difference? Only time will tell. Can the Steelers pass rush come alive against a struggling Saints offensive line? The Steelers' pass rush has long been the strength of their defense, but they haven't been as effective on a down-to-down basis this season. According to Sumer Sports , Pittsburgh ranks just 23rd in pressure percentage at 37.4%. They do rank ninth in sacks with 16, so they have managed to get the QB on the ground at an above-average level. Still, they aren't causing as much disruption as they need to be, considering the names in that group. T.J. Watt has cooled off after a hot start, Alex Highsmith isn't having his best season, and Nick Herbig has made splash plays but hasn't been as dominant as he was last season. The interior has been hot and cold, with Cam Heyward remaining a consistent presence while the other pieces have been hit-or-miss. With the Saints missing star left tackle Kaleb Banks, this is an opportunity for them to really hit their stride. If they don't, it may be time to worry. The AFC North race is heating up, and as crazy as it sounds, the Cleveland Browns lead the division, something nobody could have predicted before the season. The entire division is over .500, and three teams are 4-2. Every game is critical, and the Steelers look to continue their winning streak with a win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Steelers open as three-point favorites despite the neutral site. The Saints are coming off a victory of their own after a furious comeback attempt by the New York Giants, and J.J. McCarthy fell just short. The over/under is 44.5, and Steelers moneyline odds sit at -174. The line will move with injury news from both teams, but this feels right. On the one hand, the Saints offense is a handful, but the defense, aside from Chase Young and a few other players, is vulnerable. The key will be getting off to a faster start on offense and defense. At the beginning of the Tampa Bay game and for much of the game, the Steelers felt stuck in neutral. The offense and defense kicked it into gear down the stretch and snatched victory from the jaws of defeat. Rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard was fantastic and has quickly earned the trust of Aaron Rodgers. Trust me, that isn't easy to earn. Rodgers and Bernard looked like Rodgers and Cobb from the Packers days. D.K. Metcalf turned in a big game and made critical plays down the stretch. While the receiver room gets healthy, the two receivers will need to continue making plays. Jaylen Warren slowed down off his torrid pace, but Rico Dowdle was effective on Sunday. Still, at the end of the game, Warren was the one making big plays in overtime. It's the NFL and every game is difficult, but the Steelers need this one and Vegas believes they will get it done. Dowdle, who signed with the Steelers in March 2026, was coming off consecutive 1,000-yard seasons with two different teams: the Dallas Cowboys (2024) and Carolina Panthers (2025). away.headline: Steelers' TJ Watt pops up on injury report with new concern
away.blurb: The former Defensive Player of the Year didn’t practice on Wednesday for a rest designation. But, then he was limited in practice on Thursday because of a calf injury. This is a new injury to the public. There was some good defensive news coming out of the Steelers’ injury report, though. Cornerback Jalen Ramsey was limited on Thursday after not practicing the day prior with a wrist injury, so that was improvement. Outside linebacker Alex Highsmith was also limited with a groin issue, the same designation as Wednesday. Related Articles Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Pittsburgh Steelers haven’t been able to catch a break from injuries the last few weeks. It seems like a new star player is being added to the injury report each week. Thursday’s injury report included a surprising name, one that Steelers fans wish wasn’t on the list: edge rusher T.J. Watt. It’s unclear when or how Watt suffered the calf injury. But, now there’s a possibility, even if just a slight one, that Watt could miss Sunday’s game in Paris against the New Orleans Saints . Watt being absent for a game is always a loss for the Steelers. He can always make big and important plays for his team. Through six games this season, Watt’s recorded 4.5 sacks (tied for eighth in the league), 15 tackles, one interception, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery. Veteran tackle Cameron Heyward didn’t practice Wednesday or Thursday for rest designations, but he should be good to go come Sunday. Safety DeShon Elliott recorded his second-straight full practice on Thursday, meaning he’ll likely play on Sunday. It would mark Elliott’s first game since last October after he suffered an MCL sprain, hyperextended knee and a hamstring injury. Philadelphia Eagles star quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to be done for the season after being diagnosed with blood clots in both his lungs and deep vein thrombosis. Now, with Hurts done for the year, the Eagles are being linked to a trade for a Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback. In a recent article for Bleacher Report , Kristopher Knox named the Eagles as a potential suitor for Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph. "Mason Rudolph remains the most logical trade target for teams seeking a backup quarterback or spot starter midseason. He's one of three reserve QBs that the Pittsburgh Steelers have behind Aaron Rodgers, along with Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar," Knox wrote. "Potential Suitors : Miami Dolphins, Philadelphia Eagles." Rudolph is currently in his seventh NFL season and sixth with the Steelers. In 36 career NFL games split between the Steelers and Tennessee Titans, he has thrown 30 touchdowns, 22 interceptions, 4,925 passing yards, and has completed 64.3% of his passes. He has primarily been a backup quarterback during his career and could be a solid player for the Eagles to add to their group ahead of the deadline.

away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and several key players will be unavailable as Tampa Bay looks to build on last week's victory over Dallas. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb) has officially been ruled out after missing all three practices this week. Rookie Jalon Daniels will make his third consecutive start after leading the Buccaneers to their first victory of the season last Thursday against the Cowboys. The Buccaneers will also be without safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib), who did not participate in practice throughout the week. Wide receiver David Sills V (hamstring) was also ruled out despite being listed as a full participant in all three practices. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) is listed as doubtful, while linebackers SirVocea Dennis (ankle/foot) and Josiah Trotter (knee), cornerback Ayden Garnes (ankle), and running back Sean Tucker (quad) are questionable. Dennis and Garnes were full participants Friday, providing some encouraging news heading into the weekend. Pittsburgh is also dealing with several injuries, particularly at wide receiver. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have been ruled out, along with safety DeShon Elliott (knee). Wide receiver DK Metcalf was added to Friday's report with an illness and is questionable. away.blurb: Which made superstar edge rusher T.J. Watt’s sudden appearance on the Injury Report quite the concerning update. The top-paid defender missed a previous practice due to rest, but the latest report from the organization classified him as a limited participant due to a calf injury. The team did not include any type of game designation for Watt, although they did rule out wide receiver Ben Skowronek and cornerback Brandin Echols for their Week 7 matchup a day early. Watt was seen in the locker room after practice and did not seem to be in any discomfort, but popping up on the injury report during the week with a limited role usually means whatever did happened happened during practice. That could mean discomfort or something else. This is now the second star edge rusher to appear on the injury report this week. The team’s other starter , Alex Highsmith , popped up on the Injury Report with a groin injury. The injury reduced him to a limited participant in practice ahead of their international contest. Now, Watt is working through his own ailment. It’s good news that the organization hasn’t ruled him out, but how healthy he is entering Week 7 is under serious question. The matchup against the Atlanta Falcons always looked like a scheduled loss, if there ever was one. The 49ers are 3-point road favorites, with the total on the game sitting at 49.5 on FanDuel Sportsbook . A high total and a low spread hint at a coin-flip game. We’ll see if Mike Evans plays. On the outside, it makes more sense to give Evans two weeks off so the Achilles soreness goes away and allows Evans to complete a game. But Kyle Shanahan seems to be putting the ball in Evans’s court. If the veteran feels healthy enough to play, he’ll play, even if the team knows they could lose him mid-game. There’s familiarity here, as Raheem Morris takes on his old team. Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich is one of the best in the league and worked with Shanahan in Atlanta a decade ago, not to mention as Morris’s defensive coordinator. Morris will need to find a way to limit Drake London, who has the 8th-highest target share among all NFL receivers. The Falcons throw it to London over 28% of the time. London is 11th in EPA per target. Not far behind London is his teammate Jahan Dotson, who is 14th in EPA per target. Tight end Kyle Pitts is fifth in EPA per target among tight ends. Atlanta is not short on weapons, and we haven’t even gotten to their biggest threat. Bijan Robinson is second in the NFL, averaging 5.77 yards per carry. He averages more yards after contact (4.64) than a good chunk of running backs do per carry. Robinson is a walking highlight who is heavily involved in Atlanta’s passing attack. Michael Penix is limited when it comes to being mobile, so that should work in the Niners favor. If there’s one person you’d want to attempt to slow down the Falcons, it’s the coach who drafted most of these players and watched them practice for the past few years: Raheem Morris. On the other side of the ball, no team has been better against the run than the Falcons defense. They’re first in EPA per rush and sixth in rushing success rate. Atlanta has allowed the third-fewest 10+ yard runs and is seventh in the percentage of runs they stuff. They make teams one-dimensional. This will be a Brock Purdy game. The Falcons won’t blitz Purdy nearly as often as Washington does, but they get pressure with four. That’s a big difference. Atlanta is fourth in pressure rate despite blitzing 23.7% of the time (26th in the NFL). You can throw on this defense. Atlanta is 20th and 21st in EPA per pass and passing success rate. Caleb Williams carved up the Dirty Birds for over 300 passing yards a week ago. A good chunk of those came in the first half. Luther Burden and Colston Loveland had him a day. Tyler Huntley was efficient in Week 5 at Atlanta. He threw for only 201 yards, but completed 75% of his passes and threw two touchdowns. Huntley was efficient in Week 5 at Atlanta. He only threw for 201 yards, but completed 75% of his passes and threw for two touchdowns. Rashod Bateman and Zay Flowers combined for 13 receptions for 115 yards. The week before, Tyler Shough threw the ball 48 times for 286 yards. Chris Olave had 116 yards. away.blurb: There are a handful of players already ruled out for Week 7, but we could see some players back in action against the Falcons as the 49ers look to get a little healthier in time to go for a 7-0 start to the 2026 campaign. Christian Kirk trending toward return in Week 7 It's not a huge surprise to see optimism about Kirk's return for the 49ers' game in Atlanta. With Mike Evans potentially out because of Achilles tendinitis San Francisco needs reinforcements. Kirk's practice window was opened before Week 6, and now with a second week of practice in it sounds like the club is gearing up for him to come back in Week 7. Head coach Kyle Shanahan on Thursday spoke with KNBR and said Kirk is trending toward making his 2026 debut. " He looked good out there ," Shanahan said. "Talking to him he felt good, and I think he felt good last week. So it's trending in the right direction." The 49ers only open the first portion of practice to media, and neither Bosa nor Evans were on hand for the open part of the session according to reporters on site. Evans is working through Achilles tendonitis. He didn't practice leading up to Week 6 and still suited up before exiting the game late in the second quarter. For Bosa there was optimism he'd be back Thursday. Early indications are he isn't going to participate, but that could change if he comes out after media exit. Kyle Shanahan hopes Nick Bosa will return to practice Thursday Bosa has been out since Week 3 when he suffered a calf injury. The issue wasn't supposed be long-term and there was some hope he'd return for Week 6. Bosa didn't practice at all in Week 6 before being ruled out. He didn't participate in Wednesday's session, but head coach Kyle Shanahan expressed some optimism the star defensive end would be in the team's second practice of the week. "Can't go today, but hoping he'll be out there tomorrow," Shanahan said before practice. There may not be a team in the NFL more in need of a Bye week than the San Francisco 49ers . San Francisco will visit the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7, and then they'll be off for Week 8 where their injury situation could improve dramatically. We'll be keeping a close eye on the 49ers' injury updates all week. Follow along here: 49ers Thursday practice participation report Mike Evans, Nick Bosa not present for early part of Thursday practice Kyle Shanahan won't confirm Mike Evans injury severity There was a report from NFL Media's Ian Rapoport indicating the 49ers would have to manage Evans' Achilles tendonitis throughout the season. Shanahan would neither confirm nor deny that report while speaking with reporters ahead of Wednesday's practice. “We had to manage it last week and we're managing it this week," Shanahan said. "So, we'll see how the rest of the year goes.” It may behoove the 6-0 49ers to let their best pass rusher sit another week and then get the Bye before returning Week 9 at home vs. the Las Vegas Raiders. 49ers Wednesday practice participation report This article

away.headline: Kyle Shanahan Gives Major Injury Update on 49ers WR Ahead of Falcons Game
away.blurb: Injuries have depleted San Francisco's wide receiver room this season. De'Zhaun Stribling and DeMarcus Robinson landed on injured reserve, Ricky Pearsall will miss the rest of the season, and Deebo Samuel likely won't return for a few more weeks. However, head coach Kyle Shanahan said Thursday that Kirk is "trending in the right direction" to play Sunday against the Falcons. His potential return would provide a major boost to the offense, especially with Mike Evans' status in doubt. "He looked good out there, talking to him he felt good," Shanahan said. "And I think he felt good last week so it's trending in the right direction." "Yeah I think he's ready to go," Purdy said of Kirk. "Smart guy, vet guy obviously and everything like that, I think it was just more so having him come back last week practice and get acclimated with breaking the huddle, hearing the play call, having him go out and be confident against a guy in man to man coverage and stuff like that. He's good to go in my eyes, and I think he's going to come in do his job well, and hopefully I can get him the ball and we get into some situations where he can create some space and separation and make some plays for us. He's a playmaker." away.blurb: Insider Reveals Possible Timetable for 49ers Edge Rusher Nick Bosa’s Return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Insider Reveals Possible Timetable for 49ers Edge Rusher Nick Bosa’s Return They have gotten out to a 6-0 record despite being very depleted along their defensive front. Defensive end Nick Bosa, as well as Sam Okuayinonu, Alfred Collins and CJ West are currently out due to injuries, and defensive end Mykel Williams has been limited in practice this week due to a knee ailment. Bosa hasn't played since Week 2 because of a calf injury. He expressed confidence nearly two weeks ago that he would be able to return in Week 7 versus the Atlanta Falcons and possibly even in Week 6 versus the Washington Commanders. But he didn't play on Monday against Washington, and on Thursday, he missed practice for the second straight day this week, which makes it seem very unlikely he will suit up this Sunday in Atlanta. A CBS Sports reporter pinpointed when Bosa seems to be most likely to finally return to game action. "There's a high level of optimism at this point that 49ers star edge rusher Nick Bosa, who has been out since Sept. 20 due to a calf injury, will be able to return to game action Nov. 8 against the [Las Vegas] Raiders coming out of San Francisco's week, sources tell CBS Sports," wrote Matt Zenitz on X (formerly Twitter). Bosa has seven total tackles (three solo) and one quarterback hit in two games so far this year. Last season, he was limited to three games because of a torn ACL, the second one he has suffered since coming into the NFL in 2019. Robert Marvi Fri, October 23, 2026 at 4:15 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads While the San Francisco 49ers' defense has been performing well this season, they could use some reinforcements as they look to solidify their chances of winning the Super Bowl championship. After the Niners play the Falcons, they will have their bye week prior to their home game against the Raiders in early November. As depleted as they are due to injuries, they will certainly welcome that bye week with open arms and hope to be more whole against their former Bay Area rivals. When he has been healthy, Bosa has been one of the league's most unstoppable defensive forces off the edge. He has posted double-digit sacks in three seasons, and in 2022, he had 18.5 sacks while winning the Defensive Player of the Year award. Overall, San Francisco ranks fourth in points allowed but just 16th in sacks as of Thursday night. picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Browns in Week 7, Why They Won't, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI I'm all about celebrating a win, but the Tennessee Titans are coming up on a must-win game against the Cleveland Browns in Week 7. Can a previously 0-5 squad keep pushing the turnaround and secure their second straight victory? Last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts represented a new wave of promise for the Titans. But in the Browns, Tennessee will face the top team (in a three-way tie) in the AFC North. Cleveland has come on strong, and are coming to Nashville off a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. In the wake of a long-awaited win, I've got one reason the Titans will beat the Browns, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction. Will: Robert Saleh's defense takes over again Robert Saleh's defense just had their best performance of the season. Almost single-handedly, the score-stopping unit bottled up the Colts' offense when it mattered. The Titans forced multiple turnovers and forced Daniel Jones to make mistakes through the air. If Tennessee finds a way to win again this week, it will likely be due to a similar performance from the defense. Expect Saleh to send the heat once again after last week's six-sack outing. PFF has the Browns' offensive line ranked all the way down at 26th in the NFL. If the Titans' defensive line can force Deshaun Watson to unsettle in the pocket, we could be in for a similar path to victory for Tennessee. Won't: Browns get young playmakers going Oppositely, with the Titans' offense still operating at an inconsistent level, this game could get out of hand if Cleveland gets their young playmakers going. Oct 11, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Cleveland Browns wide receiver Denzel Boston (12) scores on a touchdown reception during the fourth quarter against New York Jets cornerback Brandon Stephens (21) at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Guys like Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion in the Browns' WR core are the sort that can change a game, and fast. Harold Fannin is one of the best rising TEs in the league, too; Cleveland has options, and offensive-minded head coach Todd Monken has led them to a surprising 4-2 tally as a result. Guys like Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion in the Browns' WR core are the sort that can change a game, and fast. Harold Fannin is one of the best rising TEs in the league, too; Cleveland has options, and offensive-minded head coach Todd Monken has led them to a surprising 4-2 tally as a result. Tennessee's defense needs to set the tone early. If the Browns come out swinging, and the Titans' offense takes as long as usual to get into any kind of rhythm, the team could be facing another steep halftime deficit. I just don't like their odds to overcome that two weeks in a row, even if this game is in Nashville. Prediction: Titans win, 17-14 However, I don't believe the Titans will have to worry about that. I'll err to to the positive side with my prediction (something I could be accused of doing too often) and say that Saleh's defense has another big game on the way to a Titans win. This team hasn't won two straight games since Weeks 10 and 11 of the 2022 season. That's a vile streak, but after last week's victory, now feels like the perfect time for Tennessee to break it. Saleh finally has his legs under him as a head coach with this team. The Browns haven't scored more than 13 points in two weeks. In front of a potentially revamped home crowd, the stars are aligning for a home upset for Tennessee. I don't believe the offense will take any major strides, but in Week 7, maybe they won't have to. I predict a narrow Titans win over the Browns. Published Oct 21, 2026 LANE MILLS Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. picks.blurb: 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 Andrew Harbaugh, Browns Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 2:55 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns march into Week 7 with an AFC North division lead and momentum behind them again. They are starting a softer stretch of the schedule but remain focused on the task ahead, which is the Tennessee Titans. Despite winning their first game in Week 6, the Titans are better than they have played. The Browns can win this game, though, if they keep up their defensive aggressiveness and make significant second-half adjustments. Todd Monken and his staff have risen to the occasion in every game, but this could be their first complete game in 2026 if they execute the way they are capable of. We said this is a poor Titans team, but there is still a game to be played, and we have some bold predictions to share ahead of it. Jared Verse gets his first sack of the season This is a wild thing to think about, but heading into Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans, Jared Verse is without a sack this season. Equally, Myles Garrett has also gone without a sack, but he has been on injured reserve. Fair or unfair, Verse is going to be linked to Garrett, and that means expectations will always be high. The Titans' offensive line is not the best unit, they are going to give up pressures, and it is time for Verse to capitalize on that. Jerry Jeudy finds the endzone Jerry Jeudy has seen him get more and more reps and big-time targets since Week 4 against the Pittsburgh Steelers. In Week 6, he made a pivotal catch-and-run that set up the game-winning field goal by Andre Szmyt. Deshaun Watson and Todd Monken have spoke highly of Jeudy this past week and he seems poised for another boost to his role. In Week 7 against he Titans, he can take advantage of their poor secondary and find the endzone for the first time this season. Browns secure at least five sacks Titans quarterback Cam Ward has had a rough start to the season and it has Tennessee sitting with a record of 1-5. He has a tendency to hold onto the ball, be reckless with it, and I think that has the Browns poised to have a big week on the defensive side of the ball. You cannot always count on turnovers, but you can count on Mike Rutenberg being aggressive on defense. One way he will do that is by getting after Ward, and I think that is where the Browns are most productive in the form of securing at least five sacks. home.headline: What Robert Saleh said about Jordan Elliott situation, response from Titans and NFL
home.blurb: "The (defensive line) room is really close," Saleh said. "For JFM to go out there and kind of help Jordan through with whatever he was dealing with at that moment I thought was really admirable on JFM’s part." The incident, which is under review by the NFL, followed a practice altercation with teammate JC Latham. Teammate John Franklin-Myers was credited with de-escalating the situation before it worsened. Tennessee Titans coach Robert Saleh confirmed on Oct. 21 that Jordan Elliott pulled a gun in the team facility's parking lot after a practice altercation last week, leading to the defensive tackle's release this week. An NFL spokesperson told The Tennessean on Oct. 21 that the Titans "promptly" notified the league about the matter, and it is under review. Saleh praised the organization and the NFL's response to the incident, citing a "pause" by the team and the league in getting Elliott assistance for what Saleh called a sign for "a cry for help" instead of involving law enforcement. "And the reason why I think the NFL and the organization did an outstanding job is because this is a man who is father, a great husband. He’s never committed a crime in his entire life," Saleh said. "And he pulled a gun in the parking lot. And the first question that I think everyone forgets to ask is why would a great man, a great father, a man who shows up on time every day, works his ass off every day, contributes the way he's supposed to contribute, is well-liked in the locker room — Why did he go off the rails and grab a gun? "And to me, those are small signs of a cry of help. In terms of, obviously there’s something greater happening. And I thought the team and the NFL did an outstanding job with regards to pausing and asking those questions and checking every single box with regards to getting him the help that he needs." Saleh vouched for Elliott's character despite the incident. The veteran defensive tackle with seven seasons in the NFL played for Saleh in San Francisco last year before joining the Titans in free agency in the spring. "These kids go through a lot. A lot. And... I will stand on the table for Jordan’s character," Saleh said. "Unfortunately, rules are rules with regards to guns on property. And sometimes it’s far greater than the knee-jerk reaction of kicking somebody when they are down. "My message to 31 other teams would be if you need a helluva run-stopping defensive tackle that can help you on a playoff run, give me a call. I’ll tell you everything you need to know about him. He’s a good man. Had a terrible lapse in judgement that I recognize as a call for help more than a criminal act." What happened with Jordan Elliott at the Titans' facility? Elliott attempted to retrieve a gun from his vehicle after a practice altercation with JC Latham on Oct. 15, according to multiple reports. home.headline: Tennessee Titans' Alontae Taylor responds to surprise benching
home.blurb: Tennessee invested heavily in Taylor and projected him as a full-time outside cornerback in the new system, a role he'd take on for the first extended period of his NFL career. That transition hasn't gone smoothly so far, and it appears the “reset” head coach Robert Saleh talks about may include a return to a nickel role. Taylor is clearly frustrated by the decision, though he said he wouldn’t change his decision to join the Titans organization and will keep showing up and doing everything he can to get back in the lineup, while hinting at a possible return to the slot. “Yeah, I was told that I would come here to play corner. Um, and that’s what my mentality was. Um, but now, um, things are changing, and I’ll just adapt," he said, while also pointing out the scheme is “different than anything I’ve played.” Amid talk about Jordan Elliott on Wednesday at the Tennessee Titans facility, cornerback Alontae Taylor sat down to discuss his unexpected inactive-day listing for Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts. Yes, the move would frustrate the Tennessee native, who is now playing for the Titans, but in the long term, it could be the best thing for both Taylor and the Titans. Taylor is a tremendous nickel cornerback, and that role is essential in every NFL defense; those players are hard to find. Time will tell if it was the right decision for Taylor and the organization. It seems like every week a big favorite is being upset, and Week 6 had two of them as the Los Angeles Rams (12.5-point favorites) lost outright at home to the Arizona Cardinals while the Indianapolis Colts (seven-point favorites) lost an AFC South battle with the previously winless Tennessee Titans. So, if you’re still alive in Survivor heading into Week 7, you deserve a ton of credit. The SI Betting team was banged up in Week 6, as managing editor Peter Dewey came up short with his Colts pick. On the bright side, those of our readers that tailed senior editor Iain MacMlllam, the New England Patriots improved to 19-2 in their last 21 home games against the New York Jets with a victory on Sunday. The Patriots have won three games in a row and are suddenly back in the mix to earn the top seed in the AFC this season. Week 7 doesn’t feature a ton of obvious Survivor spots, as the Houston Texans (9.5-point favorites against the New York Giants), Minnesota Vikings (5.5-point favorites against the Colts) and Rams (5.5-point favorites against the Las Vegas Raiders) are the three teams favored by the most on Sunday. So, Survivor players are going to have to at least consider a closer game to keep themselves alive. Here’s a quick recap of the Week 6 picks before we share our Week 7 selections. NFL Week 6 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Indianapolis Colts (L) Iain MacMillan: New England Patriots (W) It wasn’t a perfect week in these picks, but as always we’ll allow Dewey to “buy back in” so we can share differing perspectives each week in these picks. Week 7 may be the toughest week of the season, as some quality teams (Buffalo, Jacksonville mainly) are on the bye. Washington and the Los Angeles Chargers also won’t play in Week 7. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 7 Survivor Pool Picks New York Jets Geno Smith and the New York Jets are off to a 2-4 start, but they’ve been competent so far this season. Not only are the Jets 4-1-1 against the spread, but they rank sixth in the NFL in opponent yards per play and are 10th in EPA/Play on defense. The offense isn’t nearly as good (19th in EPA/Play, 22nd in yards per play), but the Jets have a very favorable matchup against a winless Miami Dolphins team – at home – in Week 7. Miami is coming off a bye, but it has just one game all season where it’s scored more than 13 points. The Dolphins rank 28th in EPA/Play, 27th in success rate and 22nd in yards per play allowed through five games this season. While I don’t believe either one of these squads is a playoff team, the Jets have a much higher floor with Geno Smith under center. New York has also hung around with playoff contenders like Green Bay, Detroit and New England while beating a 4-2 Cleveland team in Week 5. I have no faith in this Miami team, which seems destined for a top-three pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Miami had a backdoor cover against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 5, but it has relied on garbage time to get back into games that never were really close to begin with. With De’Von Achane out for the season, Malik Willis doesn’t have enough help to really get this offense going, and now he has to take on a Jets unit that has been one of the better ones in the NFL. Since the Texans are the only big favorite on the board this week – and they're just 2-4 themselves in 2026 – I don’t mind taking a shot on the Jets. I can’t imagine another spot (outside of their road game vs. Miami) where I’d really feel comfortable taking them in Survivor. – Peter Dewey Minnesota Vikings Despite the Minnesota Vikings being undefeated so far this season, this might be the last week I'd feel confident taking them. They're fresh off a bye week and have arguably the best defense in the NFL. That very same defense is going to be able to put Daniel Jones and the Indianapolis Colts' offense in a blender. It's clear by now that the key to beating the Colts is stopping Jonathan Taylor, and the Vikings rank in the top three in virtually every single run defense stat. picks.headline: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions as Kyle Murray & Co. Host the Colts in Week 7
picks.source: Minnesota Vikings On SI on MSN
picks.blurb: The Vikings will host a game at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday for just the third time this season as they welcome the 2-4 Colts to the Twin Cities in Week 7 . Minnesota looks to remain undefeated coming off an early Week 6 bye, while Indy will be scratching to salvage a start that has already led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard . Needless to say, these are two teams currently heading in completely different directions. With a beast of a November schedule looming, here are my predictions for a Vikings team looking to put together a dominating performance. 1. Kyler Murray will rack up 300-plus yards between the air and ground While the early bye provided desperately needed injury relief for the Vikings, there are fair concerns that the break may have disrupted the progress Kyler Murray and the passing game were starting to make. Murray’s performance in New Orleans was especially promising, mainly due to the fact that the offense entered the game without wideout Jordan Addison and left tackle Christian Darrisaw, and then lost tight end T.J. Hockenson to a concussion early. With all three looking to return this weekend, I see Murray having his best day yet in purple. Indy’s 351.2 yards allowed per game rank ninth in the league, and Murray’s abilities through the air and on the ground make him especially hard to stop (h/t: Ian Hartitz). After totaling 280 total yards against the Saints (229 passing, 51 rushing), I predict Murray will finish with over 300 total yards on Sunday. 2. Vikings' offense explodes for over 30 points The Vikings’ season started with a bang, scoring 39 points in the season opener against the Packers. Since then, they have not scored more than 23 points in a game. Sunday is the perfect opportunity for that to change. The Colts have given up 27.3 points per game so far this season, the sixth-highest average in the league. Minnesota, meanwhile, is looking for its first truly dominant offensive showing as it prepares for the hardest stretch of its schedule. The returns of Hockenson and Addison should open up passing options, and Jordan Mason’s possible return to the backfield could elevate a run game that Aaron Jones has carried almost entirely on his own so far. The Vikings’ offense needs to prove it can score consistently before facing some of the league's toughest opponents, and the Colts’ shaky defense may give them plenty of opportunities. 3. Harrison Smith wakes up and snags his 40th career interception Franchise legend Harrison Smith has had a relatively quiet start to his 15th NFL season . Smith announced his return a week before the Vikings kicked off their 2026 campaign and has mostly been a rotational piece in defensive coordinator Brian Flores’s ever-evolving defense. Even though “The Hitman” is clearly past his prime, he’s still one of the smartest defenders in the game, and I expect that to pay off this weekend. Smith recently confirmed to Richard Sherman that this will be his last season , so there is no better time to snag his 40th interception than now (h/t: "Richard Sherman Podcast"). Colts quarterback Daniel Jones has thrown six interceptions this season, tied for the third-most in the league , and anyone who's watched him through his career knows he’ll eventually throw a duck or two (h/t: NFL). Smith’s football IQ and Jones’s occasional recklessness may just be the perfect combination to get the NFL’s active interception leader his next pick. picks.blurb: 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7 Cole Smith, Vikings Wire Thu, October 22, 2026 at 3:55 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings enter their Week 7 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts looking to extend the league's longest winning streak. Since Week 14 of the 2025 season, the Vikings have won 10 straight games, building a 5-0 record going into last week's bye. They face a 2-4 Indianapolis team that fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday, one day after losing 26-20 to the previously winless Tennessee Titans. Head coach Shane Steichen is still employed , but the Colts feel combustible right now, with rumors of trading away star players like RB Jonathan Taylor and G Quenton Nelson swirling. Minnesota can't afford to overlook Indianapolis if they want to keep pace with the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers. But this feels like an opportunity for the Vikings to jump on an inferior team that is going through organizational changes. Here are three bold predictions for the Vikings when they host the Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday. Jordan Mason will run for 100+ yards and 2 touchdowns Jordan Mason appears to return to the lineup after missing the past four games with a thumb injury that landed him on injured reserve. Kevin O'Connell told Paul Allen on Tuesday that he expects to see Mason, Jordan Addison, T.J. Hockenson, and Christian Darrisaw back at practice on Wednesday . With Mason back, Minnesota can return to its 1-2 punch with Aaron Jones. Indianapolis enters Week 7 as one of the league's worst run defenses. They rank 22nd in rushing yards allowed, but their 4.8 yards per run allowed is tied for 5th-worst in the league. Their 12.3% stuff-rate ranks 30th in the league, and they rank last in EPA/run allowed. I expect the Vikings to stay committed to the run game and give Jones some relief after he carried the ball 85 times for 370 yards from Weeks 2 to 5. Mason averaged 3.5 yards after contact per carry in 2025, tied for 11th-best in the league among qualifying running backs. I see him breaking 100 yards and reaching the end zone twice on Sunday. Jauan Jennings will catch a touchdown pass Trade rumors swirled around Jauan Jennings in the days after Minnesota's 23-13 win over the Saints in Week 5. He was caught on camera slamming his fist into the ground following Myles Price's fumble that was returned for a touchdown. That came two plays after Jennings appeared to get open for a potential touchdown, but Murray instead threw an incompletion to Tai Felton. One play later, Murray slightly overthrew Jennings in the end zone. Jennings has caught only two passes for nine yards this season, but the rumors of a potential trade seem to have died down. He's gotten open enough that he should be getting more targets, but look for him to find more separation downfield, with Justin Jefferson, Addison, and Hockenson potentially back this week. With extra attention on the other weapons on the field, Murray will make up for his red zone misses against the Saints. The Vikings will sack Daniel Jones 5+ times and pick him off multiple times This will be the first time Daniel Jones plays against the Vikings since spending the end of the 2024 season with them. He signed with the Colts last year and played well until a fractured fibula in Week 12 slowed him down, and an Achilles tear ended his season two weeks later. He completed 68% of his passes for 3,101 yards (8.1 yards per attempt), 19 touchdowns, and eight interceptions. Jones hasn't been as efficient this season, completing 59.6% of his passes and averaging 5.9 yards per attempt, with four touchdowns and six picks. He has been pressured on 42.1% of his dropbacks, tied for the league's 7th-highest mark. Of course, no one pressures quarterbacks as much as Minnesota does. They have a league-high 47.8% quarterback pressure rate, spearheaded by a 67.0% blitz rate that is 24.5 percentage points higher than the next-closest team. Look for the Vikings to get after Jones all day and force him into turnovers. This article originally appeared on Vikings Wire: 3 Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Colts in Week 7

picks.blurb: NFL Expert Picks: Vikings Picked by Most Against Colts in Week 7 Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS U.S. BANK STADIUM VIKINGS FOUNDATION YOUTH PROGRAMS INTERNATIONAL MY VIKINGS ACCOUNT Press Releases Sam Thiel Contributor In a league governed by 17-game grinds and divisional rivalries, interconference opponents sometimes feel like passing ships in the night. But across six decades of Minnesota Vikings football, one cross-conference foe in particular has acted less like a casual visitor and more like an ultimate inflection point: the Colts. Before Minnesota hosts Indianapolis at noon (CT) Sunday, a look back at the franchise vault reveals an undeniable trend: When the Vikings play the Colts, trajectory shifts follow. In 1969, after the Vikings dropped a one-point contest at the Giants (while facing their former and, later, future quarterback Fran Tarkenton) in the season opener, Minnesota returned home to battle the (Baltimore) Colts. The Vikings scored 52 points — tied for the second-most in a game in franchise history — and the 38-point victory ignited a 12-game win streak that remains the second-longest in franchise history (regular-season games only). Minnesota went on to win the NFL Championship that season before falling in Super Bowl IV to Kansas City. Fast forward to 2022, when Indianapolis — in its fifth game under Jeff Saturday as interim head coach after the Colts fired Frank Reich midseason — traveled to Minneapolis to take on the Vikings in Week 15. After failing to clinch the NFC North title the week prior in Detroit, Minnesota dug itself into a massive 33-0 halftime deficit. The Vikings continued fighting, however, outscoring the Colts 36-3 in the second half to force overtime. In OT, Greg Joseph connected on a game-winning 40-yard field goal, helping the Vikings not only win 39-36 and secure the division, but also complete the largest comeback in NFL history. Then, just two seasons ago in 2024, the Vikings started the year with a 5-0 record. Following a Week 6 bye and back-to-back losses against the Lions and at the Rams, Minnesota hosted Indianapolis looking to get back on track. The Vikings went on to defeat the Colts 21-13 on Sunday Night Football , sparking a nine-game win streak. As Kevin O'Connell's squad welcomes Indianapolis (and former quarterback Daniel Jones) to U.S. Bank Stadium, the Vikings will try to win their 11 th consecutive contest. That led to the firing of General Manager Chris Ballard. Maybe that gives the Colts a bump. Beating the Vikings defense will mean a lot of [running back] Jonathan Taylor. I think we see that as the Colts keep it close but just miss out on the upset. Vikings 28, Colts 18 – Bill Bender, Sporting News The Colts had issues protecting Daniel Jones against the Titans in Week 6. That won't get any easier against Minnesota in Week 7. The Vikings will turn up the pressure with Dallas Turner, who has 5.5 sacks. Kyler Murray had a 76.2% completion percentage in two starts with the Vikings before the bye week. Vikings 20, Colts 10 – Vinnie Iyer, Sporting News The Vikings will be on upset alert after a bye week with the Colts on the brink of making bigger changes after firing GM Chris Ballard. But Minnesota's defense can bring some sophisticated blitzes to keep former Viking Daniel Jones slumping. Indianapolis won't get much going other than Jonathan Taylor again this week. 5 of 5 experts pick the Vikings, NFL.com Analysis from NFL.com's Bobby Kownack: The last time the Colts made a big midseason change, firing Head Coach Frank Reich and replacing him with former player Jeff Saturday in 2022, they defeated the Raiders in their very next game. Will history repeat itself on Sunday after the Colts fired General Manager Chris Ballard following their loss to the previously winless Titans? No. No, it will not. The Vikings have too formidable a defense, and the Colts have too many shortcomings on both sides of the ball, for that to happen. Minnesota is stout against both the run (fifth in yards allowed) and pass (third), increasing the probability that Daniel Jones encounters big problems should Brian Flores' defense slow down Jonathan Taylor. The Colts QB has done little this year to show he's the same guy who appeared to have revived his career with Indy before tearing his Achilles last season. He's thrown for just four touchdowns and six interceptions, and with four fumbles is exactly the type of quarterback the Vikings could feast on. Kyler Murray also seemed to settle in more in Week 5 against the Saints, posting his best completion percentage (80%) and passer rating (109.6) as a Viking. Now, he's coming off a bye to face a bottom-10 defense. 6 of 7 experts pick the Vikings, Bleacher Report Bleacher Report analysis Moe Moton: The Indianapolis Colts fired General Manager Chris Ballard, but that won't improve Daniel Jones' passing efficiency or patch up the team's 27th-ranked scoring defense. The Minnesota Vikings had extra time to prepare for this matchup, off a bye week. Also, Kyler Murray looked sharp in the Vikings last outing, throwing for 229 yards and a touchdown with an 80 percent completion rate. Assuming Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson are healthy, Minnesota beats the struggling Colts by at least a touchdown. Bleacher Report analysis Brent Sobleski: Sunday's outing against the Vikings is the Colts last gasp before their season could unofficially come to a close. Chris Ballard's ouster as general manager became inevitable after Indianapolis' embarrassing loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans. Furthermore, the Colts could quickly become sellers at the trade deadline if something doesn't change over the next three weekends. Meanwhile, the Vikings are undefeated and at home. However, they're facing a desperate team that will likely bring its best to the table. 8 of 8 experts pick the Vikings, The MMQB 11 of 11 experts pick the Vikings, ESPN 7 of 8 experts pick the Vikings, The Athletic The Vikings and Colts have met 28 times, including once in the postseason, with Indianapolis holding an 18-9-1 advantage in the all-time series. All nine of Minnesota's victories against the Colts have come at home, including five consecutive meetings from 1969 to 1997. Prior to its two recent victories over the Colts, Minnesota had dropped six consecutive games against Indianapolis from 2000-20. Battling the Bye Since the 1990 season (when the bye week was officially implemented into the schedule), the Vikings are 22-15 all-time in games immediately following a bye, including a 12-5 mark at home. From 1990 to 2009, Minnesota was dominant in post-bye contests, going 17-4 (the Vikings had two bye weeks during the 1993 season). During the past two decades, however, the bye hasn't been kind to Minnesota; the Vikings have won just five times in such games (2015 against Kansas City, 2017 at Washington, 2020 at Green Bay, 2022 against Arizona, and 2023 at Las Vegas) and have lost the past two games right after the break. away.headline: Colts' Week 6 injury report gives fans every reason to expect a Titans win
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts must feel pretty good about their health because they released Darius Slayton even though the team has struggled with wide receiver injuries this season. Not so much in Week 6, even though Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is going to be out and Alec Pierce still is . The positive is that Indy has a bye week, also known as having a matchup against the Tennessee Titans. As for Alec Pierce, no timeline exists for when he might return after reinjuring his heel. That might not happen until midseason, and the Colts will probably have far tougher games than the Titans before Pierce comes back. Besides Dulin, the only Indy player who will miss the game, according to head coach Shane Steichen , is linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs), but both Carlies and Dulin missed Week 5, and the reason the team lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers had nothing to do with the absences of Dulin and Carlies. The reason was that the defense was terrible again. Therein lies the difference between the Steelers and the Titans, as no matter how bad Indy's defense can be at times, Tennessee doesn't have the offensive talent that Pittsburgh has. Indianapolis Colts should be healthy enough to easily defeat the Tennessee Titans in Week 6 The Titans are 31st in the NFL in yards per play (4.5), last in points scored (58), 28th in quarterback rating (77.2), and 27th in rushing yards per game (82.6). Unless Indianapolis was without defensive lineman DeForest Buckner, cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, and most other good starters, Indianapolis should be able to outscore Tennessee easily. And Buckner, Ward, and Gardner are healthy and will play in Week 6. The Titans haven't beaten Indianapolis since October 2022, a stretch of six straight wins for the Colts, and Indy has no excuse for not making that seven straight victories at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday. Injuries won't be a problem for the Colts, at least heading into the game. Tennessee won't have starting safety Kevin Winston Jr., but otherwise they are mostly healthy. They just don't have a lot of talent. They haven't defeated any AFC South team since January 2024, and if that changes against the Colts in Week 6, Indianapolis needs to make some immediate changes. Ultimately, Sunday should be a get-healthy game for the Indianapolis Colts as far as record and standing in the division. When all else is going on, at least Indianapolis can count on two wins every season against the dismal Tennessee Titans . away.headline: Colts key playmaker remains sidelined with injury
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts are coming off their second-straight and fourth total loss of the 2026 season, and it’s safe to say a large reason why is because they were without one of their top playmakers. Unfortunately, his return to the field remains unknown. The Colts selected Warren with the No. 14 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Penn State, where he won the John Mackey Award as the nation’s top tight end in 2024. Related Articles Bears React to NFL Announcement for QB Caleb Williams Following His Return According to Myles Simmons of Pro Football Talk, Colts second-year tight end Tyler Warren was still sidelined on Wednesday with a groin injury. It’s certainly not the news Colts fans were hoping to hear as the team is schedule to take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. However, head coach Shane Steichen did provide a bit of a promising update after practice. “He’s progressing really well, but I’ll defer to the injury report this week on a lot of those guys,” Steichen said . It can’t be understated how much Warren means to the Colts’ offense. Despite missing Week 6, he still leads the team with 30 catches to go along with 213 yards and two touchdowns. In the meantime, the Colts will have to continue relying on veteran wide receivers Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell as well as backup tight end Mo Alie-Cox. It didn’t take Warren long to establish himself as one of the best up-and-coming tight ends in the league, either. As a rookie, Warren racked up 76 catches for 817 yards and four touchdowns.
