home.headline: Brian Flores’ Vikings defense can put Daniel Jones in a bind
home.blurb: Defensive lineman Jalen Redmond was one player the hosts singled out as an example of the pursuit required for that plan. Redmond can rush the passer, peel off when the ball gets out quickly and close on receivers from the inside. The Vikings need that kind of response across the defense if Jones is able to avoid the initial rush. One part of the podcast’s original setup has changed from a certainty into an injury question. Colts tight end Tyler Warren (groin) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday, but he remains listed first on the Colts’ Week 7 unofficial depth chart and had not received a game designation in the latest report. Warren’s availability matters because Indianapolis can use him as a blocker, receiver and screen-game piece. If he cannot play or is limited, Minnesota has one fewer versatile Colts option to account for. The Minnesota Vikings have a chance to make Sunday’s home game against the Indianapolis Colts a test of patience for Daniel Jones. The Colts quarterback has experience in Minnesota from his brief 2024 stop with the club, but the Vikings’ defense under defensive coordinator Brian Flores presents a different kind of pressure problem: force short throws, rally to the football and make Indianapolis repeatedly execute. Locked On Vikings After Dark co-hosts Luke Braun and Arif Hasan focused their Colts preview on that formula. In their review of True Media data, they said Jones had the NFL’s third-lowest average depth of target on plays when a blitz was picked up and did not produce pressure. Their point was not simply that Minnesota needs sacks. It was that Flores can use pressure looks to invite checkdowns, then trust the defense to limit the yards after the catch. Flores has made the blitz central to his approach, but Braun and Hasan noted that Minnesota also uses plenty of zone and two-high coverage. That matters against an Indianapolis offense they viewed as less effective against zone looks and two-high shells. If Jones immediately moves the ball to the flat, the Vikings have to turn those throws into modest gains instead of allowing easy drives to develop. The Vikings host the Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 25. home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Colts, they had some players upgraded and one added- linebacker CJ Allen. But starters Sauce Gardner, Tyler Warren, and Rigoberto Sanchez did not practice for a second straight day on Thursday, making their availability on Sunday increasingly doubtful. picks.blurb: Four Bold Predictions for Dolphins-Jets - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview Four Bold Predictions for Dolphins-Jets Mark H. Stowers Sat, October 17, 2026 at 5:47 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Miami's Oct. 25 visit to MetLife Stadium matches two limited offenses and two teams trying to define their seasons. The Jets are early 4.5-point favorites, but the Dolphins' improving rushing attack creates room for several bold predictions. Ollie Gordon II will rush for at least 100 yards. Gordon has totaled 188 yards in two starts since De'Von Achane went on injured reserve. Miami's 217-yard performance against Cincinnati should convince the coaching staff to keep the offense on the ground. New York has been much stronger against the pass than the run, which gives Gordon a favorable path to volume. Malik Willis will produce two touchdowns and no more than one turnover. This is the prediction that would change the game. Willis threw two interceptions and lost a fumble against Cincinnati, but the bye gives Miami time to reduce his difficult reads. Designed runs and play-action can turn his mobility into production while limiting risky throws. Miami will record at least three sacks. The Dolphins have only four sacks through five games, making this the boldest defensive call. Hafley's staff has two weeks to design pressure packages against Geno Smith. A healthier edge rotation and more aggressive use of linebackers could finally create the disruption missing against Cincinnati. The game will be decided by three points or fewer. The early total sits below 40 at several books. New York averages 18.6 points and Miami 14. The Jets have the stronger defense, while the Dolphins have the more productive recent running game. Neither team has shown enough passing explosiveness to create confidence in a runaway. A reasonable projection is Jets 20, Dolphins 17, but that margin leaves the upset door open. If Miami wins the turnover battle, Gordon controls the tempo and special teams avoid another disastrous start, the Dolphins can reverse the score. Bold predictions are not promises. They are matchup-based possibilities. The first three require Miami to emerge from the bye with a more disciplined offense and a more creative defense. If those changes appear, the fourth prediction should follow naturally.

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton Doubtful the Miami Dolphins (0-5) climb out of the cellar in the AFC East this season, but if they are going to, it almost has to begin with a win Sunday afternoon at MetLife Stadium against the New York Jets (2-4). For New York, Sunday offers an opportunity to take another step big picture as an organization and in the moment remain on the fringe of the playoff picture. The Jets are certainly far more competitive than they were a season ago but after a loss last weekend to the Patriots and looking at the rest of their schedule, a win Sunday at home against the winless Dolphins is paramount. They will need more from their offense, though, if they are to win as the Jets average just 18.7 points per game. Miami’s offense is scoring an average of 14 points per game but it’s worse than that for the winless Dolphins. Miami has yet to even lead for even a second in any of their five games this season. New York enters the game following a 26-19 loss to the Patriots in Week 6. The Jets fell behind early and could not overcome their mistakes despite another competitive defensive effort. Prior to that defeat, they snapped a four-game losing streak with a 17-12 win over Cleveland, showing the formula they hope to replicate against Miami: strong defense, ball control, and avoiding turnovers. The Dolphins’ most recent outing was a 31-24 loss to Cincinnati on October 11, arguably their most encouraging offensive performance of the season. Miami rallied in the second half and scored 24 points after managing only 46 total points across its previous four games, but defensive breakdowns once again proved costly as the losing streak extended to five games. Quarterback play will be one of the game’s biggest storylines. Veteran Geno Smith has provided stability for the Jets, throwing for 1,336 yards with seven touchdowns and just one interception through six games. While the Jets’ offense has not consistently produced explosive numbers, Smith has protected the football and given New York a chance to win most weeks. Not the same situation in South Beach. Miami’s Malik Willis has been underwhelming. Yes, the skill positions are lacking with the Dolphins, but the long-time Green Bay backup has to be better. Willis has thrown for 849 yards with a mere two touchdowns along with four interceptions. The Dolphins need greater efficiency if they are going to win or even lead a game. The Dolphins swept both meetings in 2025, including a 34-10 victory at MetLife Stadium last December. Let’s dive into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two in this AFC East tilt. away.blurb: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said running back Breece Hall would not practice Wednesday because of a quadriceps injury, although Hall had not been ruled out for Sunday. Braelon Allen has led New York with 314 rushing yards on 74 carries and would remain the primary back if Hall cannot play. Receiver Adonai Mitchell was expected to practice on a limited basis because of a finger injury. Left guard Dylan Parham is dealing with a knee injury. MIAMI GARDENS ― Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis was treated for an injured thumb on his right, throwing hand, but he fully practiced four days before a Week 7 game at the New York Jets . Willis did not throw at a bye week Monday practice that was open to reporters. Willis did not mention the thumb injury when he met with reporters a short time before the first Jets injury report of the week was released. "(Coach Jeff Hafley) just wanted to get us a little rest, and he wanted to get some young guys in there and see how they were progressing through this season," Willis said when asked what he was dealing with. "But, pretty good." Hafley said at the start of the week that Willis would be fine. "He should be good," Hafley said. "I mean, was he dealing with something? Yeah, I mean, we had a bunch of guys after the (Cincinnati) game that were having a Tuesday practice; usually we don't go until Wednesday. So just rested him on that, but I foresee him being good to go." Miami Dolphins injury report includes Malik Willis thumb Willis has said he hasn't been good enough in his first five Dolphins starts. So, can they extend the run to three against their division rivals? Carolina had been getting dominated by Tampa for a long time, losing nine of 10 matchups going into last season. But the Panthers finally stopped the bleeding with a 23-20 win at home in December. The Buccaneers got them back, though—winning the regular season finale in Tampa 16-14. For Sunday's bout, Pete Prisco at CBS Sports sees a nail-biter—and predicts the Panthers to come out with a one-point victory. Prisco writes: The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. The Panthers are rolling on offense as Bryce Young is in the MVP conversation. It will stay that way, but the Bucs will hang around. Pick: Panthers 24, Bucs 23 With the status of Mayfield still up in the air, the Bucs—per head coach Todd Bowles— are operating as if undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will get the start at quarterback. Daniels got Tampa their first win of the season against Dallas a couple of weeks ago. However, he's 1-2 on the year, and his numbers are not that impressive. In four starts, he's completed 61.2 percent of his passes—totaling 501 yards, three touchdowns and five interceptions. His 63.3 passer rating ranks 33rd in the league while his 45.0 quarterback rating ranks 23rd. As far as Carolina's quarterback goes, Young has entered the week as the NFL's leader in passing yards per game. Follow @ThePanthersWire on Twitter/X for more Panthers content. away.blurb: Three Pittsburgh Steelers have been ruled out for the team's Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, and five more are questionable to suit up, according to the team's Friday injury report. Two wide receivers Ben Skowronek and Roman Wilson left the team's 34-22 Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts with injures and did not return — and they won't be back this week, either. Skowronek suffered a calf injury early in the second quarter, and then Wilson injured his left hand on the final offensive drive of the first half. Wilson had a large wrap on his left hand after the game. On Monday, head coach Mike McCarthy said neither player will return to active this week. Fellow wide receiver DK Metcalf was initially listed as questionable to play after missing practice on Friday with an illness, but he has now been cleared to play. Tight end Pat Freiermuth is also questionable to play after suffering a calf injury in practice on Saturday. Strong safety DeShon Elliott remains limited in practice and will not return this week. Starting cornerback Jamel Dean was ruled out last week, but might be ahead of the curve on the initial multi-week estimate for his injury. He is listed as questionable. Running back Rico Dowdle , who is recovering from a dislocated toe on his left foot, is also questionable to make his return to the lineup, as is defensive tackle Keeanu Benton , who has an ankle injury, and defensive who has an ankle injury, and defensive back Jalen Ramsey , who has played through his broken wrist the last two weeks. A beat up Steelers defensive kept Tom Brady out of the end zone for 55 minutes and Mitch Trubisky successfully replaced an injury Kenny Pickett as Pittsburgh beat the Buccaneers, 20-18 at Acrisure Stadium on Oct. 16, 2022. Pickett threw his first career touchdown pass to Najee Harris in the first quarter, but a hit from blitzing linebacker Devin White knocked him out of the game. Chris Boswell kicked two field goals and Trubisky found Chase Claypool for a six-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter to extend the Steelers lead. With 4:45 to play, Brady finally punched through a defense that was playing without T.J. Watt , Minkah Fitzpatrick , Ahkello Witherspoon , Levi Wallace and Cam Sutton with a touchdown pass to Leonard Fournette, but Devin Bush broke up the two-point conversion attempt, and Trubisky and the Pittsburgh offense ran out the clock. Defensive run game coordinator and outside linebackers coach Larry Foote had two stints with the Steelers, playing from 2002-08 and 2010-13 after the team made him a fifth-round draft pick out of Michigan. Foote was a two-time Super Bowl champion in Pittsburgh and also won a Super Bowl LV ring as a coach with Tampa in 2021. As for the Baltimore Ravens , their kicker is on notice. These teams meet in a Week 7 AFC North clash, and here are bold predictions for the contest. The Bengals (3-2) enter the game in last place in the division despite having a winning record. That's because the Ravens, Steelers, and surprising Browns all have a record of 4-2. It should be another battle for the Ravens and Bengals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joe Burrow will riddle the Ravens' defense for 3 TD passes When the Bengals are right, they are tough on offense. And they've been cooking this year, ranking No. 9 in the NFL in points per game. Burrow is connecting on 71.4% of his passes. He has 11 touchdown passes and three interceptions. Look for him to keep the momentum going this week. But Burrow needs to take care of the football, which Zac Taylor said would go a long way in helping the Bengals win, according to Cleveland.com. "The turnovers is what screams at you," Taylor said. "That leads into field position." And Taylor said Burrow and his teammates are ready for this matchup. "It's exciting," Taylor said. "I think our guys really get fired up for this game. Not that they don't get fired up for every game, but whenever we play in Baltimore in a road divisional game, it's a fun one to get up for, and our guys will be up for it." Bengals RB Chase Brown will score two TDs One of them will be on the receiving end of a pass from Burrow. Brown will have a nice day, despite being caught in a time share with Samaje Perine, according to The Athletic. "I think we'll continually assess how that touch share between (Perine) and Chase Brown should play out," Bengals offensive coordinator Pitcher told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. "Every game's different. What type of scheme we lean into is going to factor into that. Obviously, what we ran more of yesterday leans into what Samaje does well, which is get downhill and run through contact." The Bengals haven't forgotten about their ground game. "You strive for balance when it comes to run-pass," Pitcher said. "You're always wanting to be the most balanced and versatile version of yourselves. It's like those are high-level goals that you set out to attain. But never in any given situation are we going to let a high-level theoretical goal get in the way of what it means on Sunday to win a game and what is the feedback we're getting in a game on a given Sunday." Derrick Henry will rush for 80-plus yards and a TD Henry is still smarting from last week's fumble that led to the Ravens' loss to the Browns. He took blame for the game-changing turnover , according to ESPN. "I got to take care of the ball," he said. "There's no excuses for that. I got to be better. I put the team in harm's way. I sound like a broken record with this, but I got to go back to work on it. Can't put the team in that situation." Teammate Kyle Hamilton took up for Henry. "Obviously, he's Derrick Henry, Hall of Fame running back [who] wants to hold onto the ball," Hamilton said. "He knows that. He's his harshest critic, so I'm not going to say anything ill about it. He's put us in position to win a lot of games." All of this will motivate Henry for a big game against the Bengals Ravens WR Ja'Kobi Lane will catch 5 passes and score a TD Lane looked ready to roll against the Browns in his return from injury. And he should be able to carve out a significant role in Week 7. Lane looked great in training camp. The injury short-circuited his 2026 season. But now he's back in the mix. His overall stat line could be impacted if Tyler Huntley is still at quarterback. But if Jackson is back, this could be a breakout game for Lane. Who will win the game? The Bengals should be able to outscore the Ravens in this matchup. But the key factor is Jackson. If he's back, the Ravens have a much better chance of winning. But we will still roll with Burrow, Chase, and Tee Higgins having a big game, along with Brown doing his thing. One of his teammates is anticipating a great game from him. Joe Burrow looking forward to facing Trey Hendrickson Burrow has practiced against Hendrickson many a time over the years, but the two have never been opponents in a real game before. There's no confusion on what he's expecting from No. 91, now in purple instead of orange. "It'll be fun, it'll be fun," Burrow said of seeing Hendrickson rushing at him . "I got to practice with him for a long time, and I'm sure he's excited to hit me a little bit after not hitting me for so long. It'll be fun." Hendrickson experienced the best years of his career on the team Burrow quarterbacked. The two nearly won a Super Bowl together, and almost made it back to another one a year later. Those memories are now an afterthought with undeniably high stakes in this matchup. The Bengals would like to avoid an 0-2 start in AFC North play. A loss would also drop them back to .500 at 3-3 overall. The Ravens just lost to the Cleveland Browns, and a second straight divisional defeat would set them back as well. How effectively Burrow evades his former teammate may determine the outcome in this game. Simpson is expecting greatness in Hendrickson's first chance at revenge, but Cincinnati is also looking for validation in moving on from the four-time Pro Bowler. away.headline: Ravens list 15 players on Wednesday injury report ahead of Bengals
away.blurb: Lamar Jackson was listed as limited Wednesday with an ankle injury, while Cam Jurgens was a full participant as he continued working toward his Baltimore debut. Outside linebacker Tavius Robinson did not participate because of a pectoral injury. Jackson's designation was the biggest update after he missed the opening portion of practice available to reporters. Coach Jesse Minter later said Jackson got limited work, and the official report confirmed his participation. Rashod Bateman was listed as limited with a shoulder injury after exiting Sunday's loss to Cleveland. Bateman has 16 receptions for 233 yards and a touchdown, with 11 catches producing first downs. Rookie tight end Matthew Hibner also was listed as limited with a hand injury. Hibner has five catches for 70 yards and a touchdown. Cornerback T.J. Tampa, designated for return from injured reserve, was listed as limited with rest, toe, and ankle designations. He recorded 29 tackles, two passes defensed and an interception last season. Calais Campbell joined Robinson as the only nonparticipants, receiving a rest day. Mark Andrews and Trey Hendrickson practiced fully despite hand and finger injuries, respectively. Baltimore listed 15 players overall. Thursday's practice will provide the next indication of whether Wednesday's progress carries into the remainder of Bengals week. Tampa remains on injured reserve and has been designated for return. Ravens list 15 players on Wednesday injury report ahead of Bengals - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ravens list 15 players on Wednesday injury report ahead of Bengals Glenn Erby , Ravens Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 8:38 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Ravens' first official injury report ahead of Sunday's matchup against Cincinnati brought encouraging developments at quarterback and center, along with a new concern for their defensive front. Jackson has missed two consecutive games after leaving the Tennessee matchup at halftime on Oct. 4. In four appearances, he has completed 68 of 96 passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception, posting a 119.6 passer rating. He also has 144 rushing yards and a touchdown on 19 carries. Jurgens practiced without a red non-contact jersey and was listed as a full participant with a concussion. Full participation is encouraging, though it does not independently confirm completion of concussion protocol or availability against Cincinnati. Before the trade from Philadelphia, Jurgens played 242 offensive snaps this season, including 187 at left guard and 55 at center. Pro Football Focus charged him with 12 pressures allowed, including one sack, across 146 pass-blocking snaps. home.blurb: Lamar Jackson was listed as limited Wednesday with an ankle injury, while Cam Jurgens was a full participant as he continued working toward his Baltimore debut. Outside linebacker Tavius Robinson did not participate because of a pectoral injury. Jackson's designation was the biggest update after he missed the opening portion of practice available to reporters. Rashod Bateman was listed as limited with a shoulder injury after exiting Sunday's loss to Cleveland. Bateman has 16 receptions for 233 yards and a touchdown, with 11 catches producing first downs. Rookie tight end Matthew Hibner also was listed as limited with a hand injury. Hibner has five catches for 70 yards and a touchdown. Cornerback T.J. Tampa, designated for return from injured reserve, was listed as limited with rest, toe, and ankle designations. He recorded 29 tackles, two passes defensed and an interception last season. Calais Campbell joined Robinson as the only nonparticipants, receiving a rest day. Mark Andrews and Trey Hendrickson practiced fully despite hand and finger injuries, respectively. Baltimore listed 15 players overall. Thursday's practice will provide the next indication of whether Wednesday's progress carries into the remainder of Bengals week. Tampa remains on injured reserve and has been designated for return. home.blurb: Wide receiver Colbie Young, a fourth-round pick out of Georgia, suffered a knee injury in week three and missed the Bengals' games against the Jacksonville Jaguars and Miami Dolphins. Andrei Iosivias's injury forced Dohnte Meyers into the wide receiver three role just a couple of months after receiving a training camp invite after playing in the CFL last season. Cincinnati also signed Mitchell Tinsley off the Houston Texans' practice squad. The Ravens face a significant injury report this week, as quarterback Lamar Jackson has missed the last two games, in which Baltimore went 1-1, beating the Atlanta Falcons and losing to the Cleveland Browns. Jackson has been labeled day-to-day and could return for a big divisional rivalry game. Cincinnati is 3-2 and last in the division, while the Cleveland Browns, Pittsburgh Steelers, and Ravens are all 4-2. Cincinnati is getting in much better shape injury-wise. The week before the Miami Dolphins game, the Bengals were unsure whether Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins , or Bryan Cook could play after earlier injuries. This week, they won't have to worry about which starters will play, barring any practice setbacks. Safety Kyle Dugger returned to practice after missing the last two games against the Jaguars and Dolphins. Dugger is a depth option at safety behind Bryan Cook and Jordan Battle. He has five solo tackles for the season and provides a veteran presence on the back end of the Bengals' defense. Defensive end Cashius Howell missed practice due to illness, and his status will be worth monitoring this week. If he misses one or two more days, the question will be whether he's physically ready to play against the Ravens. He's been a big contributor on the defensive line, racking up 12 pressures in his rookie year, second among all NFL rookies. Howell was one of five defensive line additions this offseason, the only one from the top three rounds of the NFL Draft. The other three, Dexter Lawrence, Boye Mafe, and Jonathan Allen, were either traded for or signed as free agents. Cincinnati is very high on Young after a great training camp, and his frame projects as a possible replacement for Tee Higgins. With injuries around Cincinnati's receivers, Young will get a good number of snaps if he returns in week seven.

And the pieces could certainly be in place for the Texans to make that third consecutive win become a reality. Their offense is looking the best it has all season after another strong performance from C.J. Stroud. The defense will have the task of facing a new starting quarterback on the other side in J.J. McCarthy , and all of that coming back on Houston's home field tends to make their chances look even better. And when looking at the Texans' betting odds heading into Week 7, it's becoming pretty clear that the sportsbooks have one obvious favorite in mind for this weekend's action in Houston. Texans Already Projected to Rout the Giants in Week 7 According to recent odds from FanDuel Sportsbook , the Texans are now listed as 10.5-point favorites (-550 ML) over the Giants in Week 7. That's by far the Texans' highest spread heading into any week they've played this season. And when looking around the league's Week 7 matchups, Houston is currently the only team listed as a favorite by more than a touchdown––let alone being a favorite by double digits. So if the Texans are projected to win by double-digits, and the total score isn't expected to reach above 43 points, that's not much of an optimistic statement from the books on how this Giants offense could fare against a Houston defensive unit that many considered among the best in the NFL heading into this season. Will the Texans Actually Dominate the Giants as Expected? Now, projections are one thing. Clearly, the consensus is starting to lean in one clear direction for this one between the Texans and the Giants. But does Houston actually have what it takes to make that double-digit victory come to fruition? Really, it all relies upon the defense. Last game against the Jacksonville Jaguars showed that the Texans' offense is starting to get into a bit of a rhythm . A ton of receivers are getting involved and making plays, the run game showed signs of life against one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL, and the offensive line even held up to zero sacks. But the Texans' defense just hasn't been as consistently elite as this team proved to be last year. That's not saying they can't find their way back to that level–– because the personnel looks virtually identical to last year outside of a select few changes. But we still need to see Houston have multiple strong weeks defensively to really have this level of confidence in their chances on Sunday. After all, the Giants have won three games as is this season. That's more than the Texans can claim for themselves, and New York sits atop the NFC East because of it. So as 10.5-point underdogs, they seem just a slight bit underrated here, simply when considering Houston's inconsistencies on defense. Maybe the Texans wind up crushing those projections anyways, but perhaps the Giants can make this game just a little bit more interesting than the odds tend to show. picks.headline: NFL predictions, Week 7: Not much faith in Giants to upset Texans
picks.blurb: NFL predictions, Week 7: Not much faith in Giants to upset Texans | Big Blue View Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A New York Giants Community Big Blue View October 23, 2026 Big Blue View Notifications Notifications Get The iOS App Sections News By/For Fans The Feed Community Guidelines Today's Trivia Betting Betting News FanDuel NFL Odds FanDuel Super Bowl Odds New York Giants Odds NFL Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search Get The iOS App Sections Expand News By/For Fans Expand The Feed Betting Expand Betting News All communities Notifications New York Giants odds BBV staff picks for NFL Week 7. How does the Big Blue View staff see Sunday’s New York Giants vs. Houston Texans game? See our picks for that game and the rest of the NFL Week 7 slate below. Bottom line up front: I don’t expect the Giants to win this game. I won’t go so far as to say that they can’t win the game, but things are stacking up against them. The Giants are, frankly, beat up. left tackle Andrew Thomas is dealing with his groin injury, right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor has his calf injury, and offensive tackle Marcus Mbow suffered a knee injury at the end of the Saints game. Cornerback Greg Newsome II, safety Jevon Holland, and cornerback Colton Hood are in the concussion protocol, and tight end Theo Johnson is still dealing with a neck injury. On the flip side, DeMeco Ryans has retaken control of the Texans’ defense, while C.J. Stroud has been playing some of the best football of his career. And though the Texans’ run game has been bad, Stroud is getting weapons in WRs Marvin Harrison Jr. and Tank Dell, while the Giants are scraping the bottom of the depth chart in their secondary. Starting J.J. McCarthy could provide a spark to the Giants’ offense and allow them to play the style of football for which they were built. But I just don’t know if that would be enough in the face of the Giants’ injuries. A win going into the BYE week would be an amazing boost and allow the Giants to keep pace in the division. And the upset could absolutely happen — football has been weird this year and we’ve seen some absolutely wild outcomes. But I’m afraid this could be an ugly one for New York. Tony Del Genio I’ve thought since before the season started that this was one of the most likely games for the Giants to lose. The Texans’ poor start made me start to reconsider. Their defense, one of the best in the NFL last year, has had a slow start. Cornerbacks Derek Stingley Jr. and Kamari Lassiter have not played up to their previous standards, so there is an opportunity for the Giants to stay in the game and pull off an upset if they can get their passing game to click. The Texans have given up more than 30 points three times. Last week Trevor Lawrence shredded them for 306 yards and 4 TDs. Alas, the strength of the Texans’ D is their pass rush off the edge, with the NFL’s best pass rusher, Will Anderson Jr., and Danielle Hunter (14 sacks and 60 pressures between them) leading the way. The Giants sadly have Andrew Thomas and Jermaine Eluemunor both dealing with injuries. If both cannot play or play at less than 100%, it may be a long afternoon for J.J. McCarthy in his first Giants start. Despite my misgivings about John Harbaugh making him the starter in this game rather than after the break, McCarthy does give them the best chance to mitigate the Texans’ pass rush. The Texans’ run defense is not formidable, but to say the least the Giants’ run blocking is not either, regardless of who the lead running back du jour is on Sunday. When Houston is on offense, C.J. Stroud got off to a bad start this season but has played much better for the past month. The Giants’ defensive back room is decimated by injury, with Greg Newsome, Jevon Holland, and Colton Hood all dealing with concussions, although Paulson Adebo is expected to be back this week. Who is going to cover Nico Collins, one of the NFL’s best big receivers, is anyone’s guess. Jaylin Noel and Xavier Hutchinson are no slouches, either, and the Giants will see Marvin Harrison Jr. for the second time after he caught his only TD of the season again them in the Arizona game. Pick : Texans David Hartman The Giants head to Houston this Sunday after a disappointing home loss to the Saints. J.J. McCarthy came out of the bullpen in the second half of that contest and the Big Blue news of the week is that McCarthy will start this game. The timing is slightly surprising given that New York has its Bye next week, but here we are, with a former Top-10 pick getting a shot at reviving his career after he failed in Minnesota. Can J.J. lead his team to victory, and keep the G-Men in first place in the division? This writer is very skeptical, although to be fair the Giants will remain in first place through Week 7 regardless of the outcome of this game. Weird, right? The plight of the once-mighty NFC East is a story for another day. Houston has some of the best defensive personnel in the NFL, led by edge Will Anderson, Jr. and corner Derek Stingley, Jr. In last year’s AFC playoffs, C.J. Stroud was a turnover machine and an absolute mess, but Demeco Ryans’s defense was suffocating and almost carried the Texans to the AFC Championship game. This season has been an inexplicable reverse, with Stroud playing out of his mind and the defense giving up a ton of yards and points, especially through the air. The Texans started 0-4 but have won their last two, including a huge win in London last week over the first place Jaguars. Don’t expect a letdown, as they’re still reeling from their horrible start, and need this game badly. McCarthy’s play last week was encouraging, but it was in mop-up duty against a bad defense that pulled some of its starters. This is a real test, and it’s hard to ignore the 2025 tape of J.J. He was that bad (hence, his fifth round price tag when New York traded for him). His mobility is a plus, and Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely have been uncoverable recently. Still, I don’t see McCarthy avoiding mistakes and playing well for 60 minutes, or the Giants pulling off the upset. Houston is a very good team, despite its losing record. Valentine’s View Whether I picked them to win or not, with the exception of the Week 2 game against the Los Angeles Rams, I have felt that the Giants have had a good opportunity to win each game thus far this season. I can’t say I feel good about their chances. I am not sure why the point spread has ballooned from 7.5 points to start the week to 10.5 as of Thursday, but I know I don’t have confidence in the Giants’ ability to upset the Texans. The Giants squandered real opportunities to win games the last two weeks, coming away with a tie and a loss in games they easily could have won. That stretch may haunt them. What I fear most, honestly, is the Texans’ defense. Houston has been middling on defense so far, but allowed the second-fewest points in the NFL last season. There is a breakout game coming. With the Giants switching quarterbacks, struggling to run the ball, and entering the game with their top three offensive tackles at less than 100%, I think that might be this week. I don’t want it to be, but I think J.J. McCarthy’s debut as the starting quarterback might turn ugly. away.headline: Giants Injury Report: Giants O-line Thinned By Injuries
away.blurb: Thomas, who has sat out Wednesday and Thursday over the past several weeks and returned to practice on a limited basis on Friday and Saturday before being cleared to play, is someone to watch this week. Last week he came out of the game just before the big fourth-quarter comeback attempt against the Saints; the veteran left tackle was visibly laboring through his groin injury throughout the game. Starting safety Jevon Holland was spotted at practice, off to the side with a trainer. Newsome and Holland have been the Giants defensive secondary’s best players so far this season, so hopefully their absences aren’t serious enough to keep them out of Sunday’s game. Speaking of the cornerback position, Newsome did not practice, but rookie Colton Hood (concussion) did. Sills, 6-foot-6 and 325 pounds, was originally an undrafted free agent out of Oklahoma State whom the Eagles signed in 2022. That season, Sills, who has played guard in his short NFL career, was one of three undrafted free agents to make the Eagles roster but only appeared in one game for Philadelphia. Giants Injury Report: Giants O-line Thinned By Injuries Skip to main content SI.COM The New York Giants will face one of the best defenses on Sunday when they travel to Houston to meet the Texans. So it was a bit alarming that on Wednesday, the team’s top three offensive tackles were not practicing. Starters Andrew Thomas (groin), Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and swing tackle Marcus Mbow (knee) were not participating in practice during the media viewing period. Eluemunor missed last week’s game as well with his injury after saying he would test it to see if he could anchor; he is also someone to watch this week. And with MBow now nursing something, the Giants could be thin at offensive tackle if he can’t play. The Texans have league sack leader Will Anderson, Jr. on one side of their formation and Danielle Hunter on the other. That would be quite the test for rookie J.C. Davis, who would presumably play left tackle; at right tackle, the Giants could potentially move Sisi Mauigoa from right guard to tackle, the position he played in college. Edmunds, Newsome Not Spotted During Media Viewing Portion of Practice Inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) and cornerback Greg Newsome II (concussion) were not spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. If Edmunds can’t go, Micah McFadden would get the start. The question then becomes who would wear the radio in his helmet: rookie Arvell Reese, the most likely candidate, or someone else. Rookie Colton Hood (concussion), receiver Darnell Mooney (neck), safety Tyler Nubin (neck), and tight end Theo Johnson (neck) were spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. Paulson Adebo’s Practice Window Opens Cornerback Paulson Adebo’s 21-day practice window is now open. If he clears, he could fill the roster vacancy left after Tuesday’s release of running back Najee Harris and defensive lineman Jihad Ward. Adebo has been on IR since Week 2

away.headline: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out?
away.blurb: The Giants ruled out safety Tyler Nubin (neck), tight end Theo Johnson (neck), and cornerback Colton Hood (concussion). WR Chris Olave (illness) didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but he was able to work on a limited basis during Friday's practice. He should play so long as that illness is behind him. DL Nathan Shepherd (illness) also missed two days of practice with an illness that's been going around the locker room. He was limited on Friday as well. CB Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) was limited on both Thursday and Friday, so don't be surprised if he's a game-time decision. RB Alvin Kamara (back) practiced on limited reps throughout the week. The Saints didn't bring up either of the two running b acks on their practice squad so it does llook like he'll play. Starting offensive linemen Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) are both questionable for the Giants, as is edge rusher Abdul Carter (calf). There's a crowd of Giants players available to play after being listed on the injury report this week: cornerback Greg Newsome II (groin), outside linebacker Malik Harrison (groin), defensive back Elijah Campbell (thumb), running back Najee Harris (ribs), tight end Isaiah Likely (foot), wide receivers Darnell Mooney (neck) and Charlie Jones (Achilles), as well as safety Jason Pinnock (concussion). As was the case last week, the following Saints players are on injured reserve with season-ending injuries: defensive tackle Bryan Bresee, running back Ty Chandler, cornerback David Long Jr., tight end Moliki Matavao, offensive lineman Dillon Radunz, and cornerback Rejzohn Wright. However, a couple of others have been designated to return after sitting out at least four games: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and veteran running back Travis Etienne Jr. are both expected to return after the bye week in November but it sounds like we won't see left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. until December at the soonest. Offensive lineman Nick Saldiveri is on the season-ending PUP list (physically unable to perform), while wide receiver Mason Tipton is eligible to return after missing four games. Tipton has not returned to practice yet. LS Zach Wood (calf) returned from injured reserve and is expected to play. The Saints don't have another long snapper on the roster. DL Davon Godchaux (not injury related/rest) OL Jeremiah Wright (concussion)

Dell ended up tearing multiple ligaments , sustained meniscus damage and dislocated his left knee in the incident. It knocked him out of the entire 2025 campaign, and he's been recovering ever since. Dell had 667 receiving yards and three touchdowns in 14 games during the 2024 campaign. The Texans selected him in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Houston. Though it's unclear if Dell will be able to compete at the same level he was at previously, considering how significant his knee injury and rehab actually was, he's finally ready to get back out onto the field. The next part of his playing career is here. It will mark Dell's first game back since he went down with a gruesome knee injury in 2024. Dell caught a deep pass from quarterback C.J. Stroud in a matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs in December 2024. But as Dell was bringing the ball in, teammate Jared Wayne dove for the ball too and accidentally crashed into Dell's left knee. Dell made the catch, and completed the 30-yard touchdown, but the injury was gruesome. He had to be driven off the field on a stretcher in what was a very emotional scene at Arrowhead Stadium. He remained in a Kansas City-area hospital overnight, and returned to Houston the next day. The injury was just the latest significant one that Dell has already faced in his career. His rookie season was cut short after he fractured his fibula just 11 games in, and he was then shot in the leg as a bystander at a mass shooting in Florida in 2024. Dell recovered from both injuries in time to start the 2024 campaign normally. Dell will rejoin the Texans at a critical time for the organization this season, too. After losing four straight to start the year, they've now won back-to-back contests entering Sunday's matchup with the Giants at NRG Stadium. They most recently rallied to beat the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday.

Next on the docket is a scrappy Arizona Cardinals bunch that just pulled a huge road upset of the Los Angeles Rams. The good news for the Broncos (4-2) is that they got the mini-bye week before heading to the desert and could get a few players back from injury and the commissioner's exempt list. Denver looks to extend its winning streak to three games after coming out of a gauntlet to start the season. The Broncos are currently -4.5-point road favorites over Arizona (2-4). It's nowhere near what it's been the last few seasons, but it also isn't horrid either. Denver needs to dominate the line of scrimmage on Sunday. Open lanes in the running game and do a better job of pass protection. It's a cliche, but success on offense starts in the trenches. Getting that could lay the foundation for jump-starting the offense. — Ian St. Clair Bench Bo Nix; Start Jarrett Stidham Just kidding. Ya'll crazy if you think benching Bo Nix is even remotely the answer. That said, Bo Nix does need to play better, and he isn't seeing the field well to start the season. He's had slow starts in every season he's played, so, for now, I'm chalking this up to another slow start. However, seven games in, I'm hoping to see him take flight a bit now that the hardest part of the Broncos' schedule is complete. At 4-2, they got through it with a winning record, and that is all we could hope for. — Tim Lynch Pressure the QB The key to this game is the same as it has been every week. Get to the QB. The defense has done a great job this season of causing mayhem in the backfield. Make it uncomfortable for Jacoby Brissett (like the back of a Volkswagen). When QBs are harassed and hurried, they make mistakes. — Adam Malnati Disciplined, execution-based offensive football This team needs to execute at a high level, and it will win this game easily. The defense is already there. If the offense can up its game, this Broncos team will be unstoppable. — Sadaraine Limit the impact of Trey McBride The Broncos defense has performed well this season, aside from a few games. For the most part, they've been able to limit the impact of the opposing team's top player on their offense. This week, they face All-Pro tight end Trey McBride, who is coming off a sensational 2025 season. He is the focal point of Arizona's aerial attack and gets over ten targets per game. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph needs to come up with a good game plan that limits his impact on the game. If they can slow him down, Denver will have a great shot at earning their fifth victory of the season. — Christopher Hart What are your keys to Sunday's game?

away.headline: Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return
away.blurb: Running back Jonah Coleman, who has been designated to return from IR with his ankle injury, practiced in full on Wednesday. Patrick Surtain II, who left the team's Week 4 game with an ankle injury, was also at practice on a limited basis: Unfortunately, Tyler Badie, Talanoa Hufanga, and Jonah Elliss all did not practice, and Elliss' injury could end up being more extended. Hufanga hurt his ankle in Week 5 against the Los Angeles Chargers, and both Badie and Elliss got hurt in Week 6 against the Seattle Seahawks. Fortunately, Hufanga's injury is minor. As for Surtain, James Palmer is reporting that the likely return for the Defensive Player of the Year is Week 8 against Kansas City, but he also didn't totally shut the door on Surtain playing this week : Him practicing in limited fashion does give him a chance to play, but you almost want to wonder if the Broncos understand the opponents they have coming up and want to ease Surtain back into things for Week 8, as that game could carry major impact across the division and conference in terms of seeding. All in all, the Broncos seem to be trending toward being more 'full strength' for the Chiefs game in Week 8. However, not only could Coleman find his way back into the lineup in Week 7, but, until he's ruled out, Surtain could be nearing a return as well. The Broncos also have wide receiver Pat Bryant on IR. He is eligible to return f in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Denver plays Arizona, Kansas City, and Carolina before the Week 10 bye, which just so happens to line up nicely with the trade deadline. This article was originally published on predominantlyorange.com as Latest Broncos' injury report indicates key players are nearing a return . The Denver Broncos have dealt with their share of injuries this year, unfortunately. The bright side though, is that the Broncos are consistently among the least-injured teams in the NFL, and the ailments this year have largely been minor. As the middle of the season approaches, the playoff race will slowly start to heat up, and Week 8 against the Kansas City Chiefs could present a legitimate playoff atmosphere. Before the Chiefs, though, the Broncos have to get by the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. And in the team's first injury report of the week, it does seem to indicate that the team could get some key players back. away.headline: Cardinals get troubling Jeremiyah Love injury update before Broncos game
away.blurb: Arizona held Love out of last week’s matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, giving the rookie additional time to recover from his ankle injury. For Love, the priority remains getting healthy enough to return without risking another setback. While Arizona has not officially ruled him out for Sunday, the latest report suggests the team may need to prepare for another game without one of its most important young offensive players. Giants DC Threatens Players Amid 'Unacceptable' Behavior, Calls Out 'Traitors' The Arizona Cardinals could be without one of their most promising offensive weapons for another week. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos as he continues recovering from an ankle injury, according to CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz. Love already missed Arizona ‘s Week 6 victory over the Los Angeles Rams, and the latest report suggests the Cardinals could be forced to play without their starting running back for a second consecutive game. The former Notre Dame standout did not participate in Wednesday’s practice, raising further concerns about his availability heading into Week 7. Love has been dealing with an ankle injury that initially surfaced following Arizona’s Week 4 matchup against the New York Giants. Although he returned to action against the Detroit Lions in Week 5, the rookie struggled to find his rhythm, finishing with just 22 rushing yards on 12 carries. Before being sidelined, Love had rushed for 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 carries through five games. He also contributed 11 receptions for 36 yards and another touchdown. Arizona selected Love with the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, making him the highest-drafted running back since Saquon Barkley went second overall in 2018. The Cardinals entered the season with high expectations for the former Fighting Irish star, who established himself as one of college football’s most explosive offensive players. Now, his early NFL career has been interrupted by injuries. With Love expected to remain sidelined, Arizona could once again turn to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to handle the rushing responsibilities. The Cardinals leaned on their running back depth during last week’s victory, but facing Denver presents another challenge for an offense attempting to establish consistency. The Cardinals have invested heavily in the rookie’s long-term future, and his availability will be an important storyline as the season progresses. away.blurb: First, the good news following the portion of Thursday's practice open to media members: cornerback Pat Surtain (limited; ankle ), wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (limited; chest ), running back Jonah Coleman (full; ankle ) and cornerback Riley Moss ( ribs ) continue to practice. Surtain might be more likely to make his game-day return in Week 8 , but getting practice reps is a step in the right direction. Jahdae Barron has been starting in place of PS2, and Taylor Rapp did a nice job helping replace Hufanga last week. Meanwhile, Coleman and outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper ( reinstated ) are both candidates to return to the 53-man roster later this week. There's mixed news on the injury front as the Denver Broncos continue preparing for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals . Now, the bad news: safety Talanoa Hufanga ( ankle ), outside linebacker Jonah Elliss ( ankle ) and running back Tyler Badie ( thumb ) remain sidelined. Hufanga is expected to miss at least one more game , and coach Sean Payton seemingly hinted after Wednesday's practice that Elliss could land on short-term injured reserve later this week. Denver's scheduled to practice again on Friday before releasing a final injury report with game statuses for Sunday's showdown with the Cardinals . All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET New England Patriots (+3) at Chicago Bears Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime This is a big game for both teams, a tough one for the road team on a short week. Both teams can score, which should make this a fun one to watch. I think the Patriots have the better defense and that will be the difference. They overcome the road to win a much-needed game. Pick: Patriots 28, Bears 27 Pittsburgh Steelers at New Orleans Saints (+3.5) Paris on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) These two are both coming off road victories and now have a long trip to play this one. The Steelers have been the more consistent team this year, but the Saints looked good last week against the Giants . This will be tight, but the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 27, Saints 26 San Francisco 49ers at Atlanta Falcons (+3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The 49ers are rolling as the league's best team, especially on offense. But losing Mike Evans will hurt. The Falcons couldn't stop the Bears last week, so what's to think they will slow down Brock Purdy ? They might not. But the Falcons will keep up. It's close. Pick: 49ers 30, Falcons 28 Cleveland Browns at Tennessee Titans (+1.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Browns are 4-2 after beating Baltimore last week, while the Titans beat the Colts last week. Neither team is doing much on offense, which suggests this will be a low-scoring game. I think the Browns have a better defense, which will be the difference. They win it again on a late field goal. Pick: Browns 17, Titans 16 Indianapolis Colts (+6.5) at Minnesota Vikings The Vikings are off a bye, while the Colts are off a terrible home loss to the Titans. That led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. Maybe that gives the Colts a bump. Beating the Vikings' defense will mean a lot of Jonathan Taylor . I think we see that as the Colts keep it close, but just miss out on the upset. Pick: Vikings 21, Colts 18 Miami Dolphins (+4.5) at New York Jets The Dolphins are off their bye in search of their first victory, while the Jets lost to the Patriots last week. The Jets have the better team and their defense should be able to limit the Miami offense. But the Dolphins play hard and will also play well on defense. It's close. Pick: Jets 19, Dolphins 17 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+3.5) at Carolina Panthers The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. The Panthers are rolling on offense as Bryce Young is in the MVP conversation. It will stay that way, but the Bucs will hang around. Pick: Panthers 24, Bucs 23 Cincinnati Bengals (+3) at Baltimore Ravens The Bengals are coming off a bye, while the Ravens are coming off a loss to the Browns. They could have Lamar Jackson back from an ankle injury here, which certainly changes things. Even if he's back, I think Joe Burrow will have a big day throwing it. The improved Bengals defense will do the rest. Upset. Pick: Bengals 24, Ravens 23 New York Giants (+10) at Houston Texans Who starts at quarterback for the Giants? It should be J.J. McCarthy , but we will see. No matter who starts, the Texans ' defense is having issues. The Giants will move the ball. But they won't stop C.J. Stroud . He's on fire and that gets the Texans the victory. Pick: Texans 27, Giants 23 Denver Broncos at Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Cardinals are coming off a big road upset of the Rams , while Denver beat Seattle last Thursday. The Denver offense has been lifeless so far this season. But the defense is still sticky. I think that defense will come up big, while Bo Nix finally makes some plays. It's close. Pick: Broncos 24, Cardinals 21 Green Bay Packers (+3) at Detroit Lions Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Lions are coming off a bye, which they needed, while the Packers are coming off consecutive victories. They are playing much better on both sides of the ball. The two defenses will be challenged here, but the Lions will be the better offense at home coming off the bye. Lions win it by a tiny margin as both quarterbacks light it up. Pick: Lions 34, Packers 33 Los Angeles Rams at Las Vegas Raiders (+4.5) This is a must-win for both teams, as they are on losing streaks. The Rams have a lot of injury issues, which have really impacted their team. They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here. But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders , who hang around. Pick: Rams 28, Raiders 27 Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) at Seattle Seahawks Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a revenge game for Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker , who was the Super Bowl MVP for Seattle last February. And let's not forget the Chiefs have Patrick Mahomes . Seattle is good on defense, but their offense is turning the ball over. That matters here. Chiefs take it. Pick: Chiefs 23, Seahawks 17 Dallas Cowboys at Philadelphia Eagles (+4.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Eagles are a mess with all the injuries, including quarterback Jalen Hurts being out for the year. The Cowboys have struggled on offense the past two weeks, which isn't a good look. This is desperation time for these two. The Cowboys will win it, but it's close. picks.blurb: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Green Bay Packers in Week 7 Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI On Sunday afternoon, the Detroit Lions will take on a red-hot Green Bay Packers team that has won three straight games. Most recently, the Matt LaFleur-led squad dispatched of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, 23-13. It marked the third consecutive game in which Green Bay held its opponent to 14 or fewer points. And on the season, the Packers’ defense – coordinated by former Arizona Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon – has allowed the 10th-fewest points in the NFL (20.8/game). Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the ball, Green Bay – led under center by sixth-year passer Jordan Love – has scored the 10th-fewest points in the game (21.2/game). Through six weeks, Love has also completed just 59.7 percent of his pass attempts. If the season ended today, it'd rank as his lowest completion percentage as a starting quarterback in the NFL. Yet, multiple Green Bay pass-catchers have flourished, most notably wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson, now in his fifth NFL season, has already amassed as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The former second-round pick secured 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago. Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already surpassed all his receiving totals from his rookie campaign. He's already racked up 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns amid a career breakout season. And just like Watson, he's well on pace for a 1,000-yard receiving campaign. Consequently, both Watson and Golden possess the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ secondary, even with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back in the fold for Detroit. In addition to Watson and Golden, the Lions will also likely have their hands full with Packers running back Josh Jacobs. The Pro Bowler returns to the lineup after spending the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner exempt list for an offseason domestic abuse incident. Jacobs, who's coming off a 929-yard, 13-touchdown rushing campaign in 2025, should provide an immediate boost to Green Bay's league-worst ground game. In case you were wondering, the Packers have compiled a measly 359 total rushing yards through the season's first six games. Expect Jacobs, along with Watson and Golden, to give Kelvin Sheppard's defense its fair share of fits on Sunday. However, at this present juncture, I'm still willing to give the Lions a 60 percent chance to pull off the Week 7 victory at home. As I do each week, I'm going to break down my favorite bets against the spread for every single game. Let's dive into my plays for the Week 7 slate. NFL Week 7 Spread Picks All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Patriots vs. Bears Spread Pick The Bears team is a completely different squad with Caleb Williams back on the field. The Chicago defense has also been much better this season than people give it credit for. Pick: Bears -3 (-102) Steelers vs. Saints The Saints have the worst run defense in the NFL, and now they have to take on a strong Pittsburgh run game. Jaylen Warren is averaging 5.5 yards per carry this season, so he should carry the Steelers to a win in France. Pick: Steelers -3.5 (-102) 49ers vs. Falcons The Falcons' secondary is banged up, and now they have to take on an MVP candidate in Brock Purdy. San Francisco's offense should be able to score at will in this game. Pick: 49ers -3 (-102) Browns vs. Titans The Browns are just a better version of the Titans. They have a slightly better quarterback and a stronger defense. The only world I'd ever bet on the Titans this season is when they're getting more than a field goal's worth of points. Pick: Browns -1.5 (-110) Colts vs. Vikings The Vikings' defense is going to put the Colts' offense in a blender. They're the best run defense in the NFL, and their ability to blitz is going to confuse Daniel Jones. As long as the Vikings' offense can score enough in this game, they should win comfortably. Pick: Vikings -6.5 (-108) Dolphins vs. Jets The Dolphins have had one of the most difficult schedules in the NFL to begin this season. This is by far their easiest opponent yet, so maybe the Dolphins will be able to put up a fight. Pick: Dolphins +4.5 (-105) Buccaneers vs. Panthers The rule with any NFC South team is: the moment you think they're good, bet against them. Let's also not forget that the Buccaneers' defense has quietly been one of the better units in the NFL this season. They can keep them in this game. Pick: Buccaneers +3 (+100) Bengals vs. Ravens Lamar Jackson is likely out for one more game, which is bad news for the Ravens as they now have to take on a Bengals team that's fresh off a BYE and has been playing some solid football on both offense and defense. Pick: Bengals -1.5 (+100) Giants vs. Texans The Texans' defense is going to get back into form, and C.J. Stroud has been playing at an extremely high level the past few weeks. I have no faith in J.J. McCarthy, so I think this is going to be an ugly game for the Giants. Pick: Texans -10.5 (-108) Broncos vs. Cardinals No team has had a tougher schedule so far this season than the Denver Broncos. Now, they get to take on a Cardinals team that ranks dead last in the NFL in net yards per play. I'm surprised this spread is set at such a low number. Pick: Broncos -4.5 (-110) Packers vs. Lions The Lions are coming off a BYE and they get Brian Branch back in their secondary, which is going to give their defense a massive boost moving forward. Now is the time to buy some stock in the Lions. Pick: Lions -3 (-110) Rams vs. Raiders The Rams' injuries may be piling up, but they should still be bigger favorites against the Raiders, who are far worse than their record indicates. Their defense has become a bottom-10 unit, and they can't run the football. The moment Kirk Cousins begins to regress, things are going to get ugly in Las Vegas. Pick: Rams -4.5 (-105) Chiefs vs. Seahawks The Chiefs may just be the best team in the NFL, while the Seahawks are struggling offensively. They can't run the football, and Sam Darnold is turning into a pumpkin. Kenneth Walker is poised for a massive game against his former team. Pick: Chiefs +2.5 (-102) Cowboys vs. Eagles The Cowboys' defense is one of the worst defenses we've seen in recent NFL history, so I hesitate to lay points on this team, especially on the road against a divisional rival, even if the Eagles are dealing with a plethora of injuries. On the other side of the image is Lions QB Jared Goff with RB Jahmyr Gibbs and a logo for the Detroit Lions behind them. Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:21 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFC North still looks like one of the NFL's most competitive divisions just six weeks into the 2026 season. Every team in the division finished with a winning record in 2025, and that trend has continued into this year . Now the Packers and Lions are gearing up for a huge divisional matchup that could have huge ramifications come playoff time. Green Bay is looking strong after a questionable start to the season. They are on a three-game winning streak after taking care of Dallas on Sunday Night Football . The Packers are still a bit behind the Vikings, but getting a win in Week 7 will get them one step closer to catching up. Meanwhile, Detroit quieted their doubters in Week 5 after crushing Arizona in the desert. The Lions even got a solid game from their defense, something that has eluded them for most of the season. But Detroit is coming off their bye week, so it is impossible to know if they'll carry over that momentum or come out flat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Which team will come out on top in this massive divisional matchup? Here are three bold predictions before the NFC North clash between the Lions and Packers in Week 7. Jared Goff throws his first interception of the season, but still shreds Packers defense Mark Konezny-Imagn Images Goff may be the most underrated quarterback in the entire NFL this season. He may look like a quarterback from a different age, but Goff can still sling it with the best of them. Detroit's franchise quarterback has 1,485 passing yards with 12 touchdowns and zero interceptions through five games. That's right, he still has not thrown an interception at any point this season. This speaks to how careful Goff is with the football, no doubt owing to his veteran experience. All of that said, this could be the week that the streak comes to an end. The Lions should not underestimate the Packers' defensive unit, even if they don't have Micah Parsons in Week 7. Green Bay has one of the better coverage units in the NFL this season despite an unproven cornerback room. Even more impressive is that they lead the NFL in interceptions with nine through the first six games. If any team is going to snap Goff's streak, it will be the packers. Goff will throw his first interception of the season against Green Bay on Sunday. All good things must come to an end, including his impressive streak of clean games. However, that doesn't mean he'll wilt against the Packers. Detroit will finish this game with at least 400 passing yards, shredding Green Bay's secondary from wire to wire. Josh Jacobs rumbles for 100 rushing yards, two touchdowns in 2026 debut Green Bay's one weakness this season has been their rushing attack. The Packers are averaging a pitiful 59.8 rushing yards per game this season. That is due to a combination of offensive line issues and a thin running back group. But the latter is about to change. Josh Jacobs looks slated to return in Week 7 after being removed from the commissioner's exempt list. "I would say Jacobs has been preliminarily cleared and is expected to play this week. He is going to practice. He's going to be on the field. They say he has kept in good shape, and the Green Bay Packers, who have had a really solid start to the season, probably could use a little bit of an improved running game, and they get Josh Jacobs in Week 7 to come in and do it," NFL insider Ian Rapoport said on Wednesday via Good Morning Football. Getting Jacobs back won't fix everything overnight. After all, it is fair to be skeptical of how ready he truly is after staying away from football for over a month. Still, Jacobs could have a breakout game against Detroit if Matt LaFleur dials up enough carries for him. Jacobs will go over 100 rushing yards and score two touchdowns against the Lions. Green Bay wins an NFC North shootout thanks to Detroit's compromised defense Mandatory Credit: Wm. Glasheen USAToday Network via IMAGN images Of course, the matchup that everyone will be watching in this one is Jordan Love against Detroit's struggling secondary. Green Bay suddenly looks capable of keeping up with Detroit's offense. The emergence of both Christian Watson and Matthew Golden has unlocked the team's passing attack. On paper, they're in the same tier as Detroit in terms of passing yards per game. The good news for the Lions is that Brian Branch is expected to make his 2026 debut against the Packers in Week 7. It is impossible to know just how good Branch will look after last season's Achilles injury . Getting him back is also no guarantee that Detroit's defense will magically play better. But it is a start. In the long term, getting Branch back should do wonders for the Lions. Unfortunately, it won't be enough to win this game. The Packers win by one score in an epic shootout at Ford Field. Related: Caleb Williams and Drake Maye are on fire. Can either defense make a stand in Bears-Patriots? Both offensive units boast elite fantasy firepower, but division clashes always bring unique defensive tests and gamesmanship. If you are navigating lineup decisions ahead of Sunday afternoon's kickoff, here is a breakdown of which Lions fantasy superstars belong in your starting lineup, and which options require a bit more caution. Must-Start Locks Amon-Ra St. Brown (WR) * Verdict: Mandatory Start (WR1) * The Outlook: St. Brown remains the unquestioned heart of Detroit's passing attack. Operating out of the slot, "The Sun God" provides a relentless target floor that thrives in fast-paced divisional battles. Green Bay's secondary has struggled at times against refined route runners over the middle. Expect Jared Goff to lean heavily on his favorite target to sustain drives, making St. Brown an elite WR1 in all PPR formats. Jahmyr Gibbs (RB) * Verdict: Mandatory Start (RB1) * The Outlook: Gibbs' dual-threat dynamic explosion makes him virtually matchup-proof. With his elite speed on Ford Field's turf, he only needs a handful of touches to break open a slate. The Packers have surrendered chunk plays to explosive pass-catching tailbacks out of the backfield, giving Gibbs immense ceiling potential in PPR and half-PPR leagues. High-Upside Starts Jared Goff (QB) * Verdict: Solid QB1 Start * The Outlook: Goff inside the friendly confines of Ford Field is one of the safest fantasy plays on the board. At home, Goff operates Drew Petzing' system with supreme efficiency and rhythm. While Green Bay's pass rush can generate pressure, Goff's quick-release capabilities and weapons across the field give him a safe 18–22 point fantasy floor with multi-touchdown upside. Start with Caution / Situational Starts Jameson Williams (WR) * Verdict: High-Risk Boom-or-Bust Flex * The Outlook: Williams possesses game-breaking speed capable of turning a single target into a 70-yard touchdown. However, against Green Bay's deep safety coverage, target volume can be volatile. If you need pure upside to pull off an upset in your matchup, roll the dice on Williams; if you require a steady double-digit floor, explore alternative options. Sam LaPorta (TE) * Verdict: Low-End TE1 / High-End TE2 * The Outlook: LaPorta continues to command valuable red-zone attention, but increased target competition across the offense has capped his weekly target share. Green Bay's linebackers and safeties play tough physical coverage against tight ends over the middle. He remains startable given the top-heavy nature of the tight end position, but manage expectations accordingly. Final Lineup Verdict Lock in your top-tier Lions stars without hesitation. Detroit's high-octane offense inside Ford Field provides plenty of fantasy production to go around. Fire up St. Brown, Gibbs, Goff with confidence as Detroit aims to defend home turf against their division rivals.

away.blurb: The Green Bay Packers have built a three-game winning streak heading into its Week 7 matchup in the 2026 NFL season, capped by a 23-13 triumph over Dallas last weekend. Despite the team's recent success, uncertainty surrounds the health of several key offensive players. Jordan Love, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden were all listed on the Packers' injury report Wednesday after taking part in practice on a limited basis. home.blurb: The Detroit Lions (3-2) and Green Bay Packers (4-2) will square off in a division rivalry game in Week 7, and both teams were back on the practice field on Thursday. On the second day this week, the Lions practiced all 51 players on their active roster, as well as the two players expected to return from injury. After a walkthrough on Wednesday, the Packers finally got one of their key offensive starters on the field for the first time this season. "He plays at a high level. He's big, he's physical, he's really smart," Petzing said of Mays. "The communication piece is a huge part of playing that position. So, that's just kind of a number of things off the top of my head, but excited to see him back out there." "We've been getting him ramped up," Packers Matt LaFleur said on Wednesday . "He's been in the building. We've been doing things with him, in terms of our strength staff, our athletic training staff. You can't simulate football until you get out there. These next two days are going to be great work for him as we ramp him up." home.blurb: In total, 10 players were listed as limited participants, while wide receiver Bo Melton still did not participate due to a back injury. LVN's name has appeared on plenty of these injury reports this season, and while he struggled at times against the Dallas Cowboys, no one can argue that he makes this defense better when he's out on the field. Keep in mind, both Christian Watson and Matthew Golden were still limited participants. Watson is dealing with an ankle injury, while Golden is going through something with his shoulder.
