The new names to appear a few days prior to the team's Week 7 showdown against the Detroit Lions were linebacker Zaire Franklin and EDGE Lukas Van Ness. Franklin, 30, was brought in this offseason after spending his first eight years in the league with the Indianapolis Colts. According to the report , Franklin is dealing with a shin injury, while LVN appeared on the list due to an illness. The team didn't officially practice on Wednesday, Oct. 21, so all of the injuries and designations listed were all estimations . Roughly 24 hours later, the Packers gave the Lions a better idea of who's struggling and who's in a good place to play on Sunday, Oct. 25. Seeing as the Lions only had three players appear on the initial injury report, it's clear these two teams are in vastly different places. Green Bay improved to 1-1 in NFC North play with a dominant win at home against the Chicago Bears, and they may have won back-to-back games at Lambeau Field, but now it's time for them to head to Ford Field to take on the Lions. On the defensive side of things, Franklin and Van Ness are joined by defensive tackles Anthony Campbell (ankle) and Jordon Riley (Achilles) and cornerbacks Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck) and Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring). For Love to see three of his receivers on the report is a bit scary, but there's still a bit of time before Week 7 rolls around for everyone to get healthy.

home.headline: Packers-Lions Wednesday Injury Report: Here’s What Jordan Love Said About Sore Back
home.blurb: The Green Bay Packers’ star quarterback, who has carried the load for most of the team’s 4-2 start, was deemed limited participation on Wednesday, the first day of on-the-field work before Sunday’s NFC North showdown at the Detroit Lions. Only one player, receiver Bo Melton (back), would not have practiced. Nine players were limited, including Love and receivers Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Christian Watson (ankle). The Lions are coming off their bye. Every player on the roster practiced, including safety Brian Branch, who is set to return from last year’s torn Achilles. Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), CB Brandon Cisse (hip), WR Matthew Golden (shoulder), QB Jordan Love (back), DT Jordon Riley (Achilles), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), WR Christian Watson (ankle), WR Savion Williams (ankle). Riley has been designated to return from injured reserve and is within his 21-day practice windows. Limited participation: CB Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring). Packers-Lions Wednesday Injury Report: Here’s What Jordan Love Said About Sore Back Skip to main content SI.COM GREEN BAY, Wis. – Jordan Love has taken a beating at times this season. For the first time, it’s shown on the injury report. He said “no” when asked if he was concerned that he will not be in the lineup against Detroit. Coming off a Sunday night game and with a Thursday night game looming against the Panthers, coach Matt LaFleur conducted a “jog-through” practice on Wednesday but will put the team in pads for a “really good” practice on Thursday. That was welcome news for Love. After two games of strong pass protection in wins over Tampa Bay and Chicago, it was another painful week for Love in the win over Dallas. “It’s just dealing with a sore back from the game,” he said. “Just some lingering effects from that. One of those things, we’ll just take it day by day but, obviously, it was nice to have a jog-through day, a little bit more mental day, and just recover.” By the official stats, Love and Cleveland’s Deshaun Watson have absorbed a league-high 45 hits through Week 6. He was hit eight times and sacked on three against the Cowboys. “Obviously, just with the back, I don’t know exactly what play it happened on, when it happened,” Love said. “We talk about all the time: You want to, obviously, limit me taking hits in the pocket. That’s something that we’ve talked about, we harp on, and there’s been some better efforts to do better and protect better. I think guys are responding to that. It’s one of those things, yeah, you want to be able to limit as many hits as I take.” Running back Josh Jacobs, who is returning after six weeks on the exempt list, is not on the injury report. “I’ve been actually practicing with my helmet and shoulder pads, so it’s not like it’s overly different,” Jacobs said. “I don’t know where we’re going to be at this week, or if I’m actually going to play or not. picks.blurb: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:41 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There is a big time injury for the Los Angeles Rams . And the Raiders have a major concern as well. These teams meet in Week 7, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. It's a crucial game for the Rams, who stand at 2-4 and find themselves a staggering four games behind the front-running 49ers in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Raiders stand at 3-3 in third place in the AFC West. They're unlikely to be a playoff contender, but are trying to build a strong foundation for 2027. Let's take a look at what could happen when these teams battle. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Matthew Stafford will throw for three touchdowns It's hard to gauge what kind of yardage output Stafford will have. Without the injured Davante Adams, the Rams may lean on the ground game a little more. Adams is the team's leading receiver with 480 yards and four touchdowns. Sure, Stafford still has Puka Nacua. And Nacua will get his targets and yardage. But who steps into the No. 2 role? Maybe the Rams will use tight end Tyler Higbee more. Or perhaps Konata Mumpfield or Jordan Whittington will step up and produce. However, despite the receiver situation, the Rams will need to find a way to get the ball into the end zone if the Raiders load up to stop the run in the red zone. So look for Stafford to spread it around and still get his TD passes. Stafford said he understands the situation , according to The Athletic. "I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win," Stafford said. "In some of those guys' instances where they're going to have opportunities to hopefully come back and play for us, make sure that when they come back and play for us, it's meaningful stuff for them." However, some observers think Stafford has finally reached the end of his NFL rope, according to ESPN. "Stafford can't move," Ben Solak wrote. "He was never the most mobile quarterback, but the Rams were willing to use him on boots in the past. In 2024, 16.8% of Stafford's pass attempts were on the run — an above-average number! That fell to 13.9% in 2025 and is down to 9.6% in 2026. Sure, designed rollouts are down — but it isn't just that. "Stafford has zero scrambling passing yards on the season per NFL Next Gen Stats. He has yet to break the pocket and complete a pass on a scramble drill. The last quarterback to log no scramble passing yards through six weeks of a season was 2022 Tom Brady — the final season of a pocket passing titan." But it's not time to write Stafford off. Rams RB Kyren Williams will rush for 90-plus yards The Rams must run the football against the Raiders, a team that struggles to stop the ground game. The Raiders are giving up 134.3 yards per game, which ranks No. 28 in the NFL. Keeping the ball on the ground needs to be a big part of the Rams' game plan. The Rams have thrown 252 passes with 148 rushing attempts. McVay wants those numbers closer together , according to theramswire.com. "Ultimately, what I care about and what we care about is what's the best way is to move the ball and score points," McVay said. "Because of some of the situations that we've been in, those two-minute situations have gotten us a little bit out of balance. No matter how I cut it, it's an excuse. I'd like to be able to have a little bit more balance. And that's reflected by being efficient on early downs and sustaining drives." One thing is for sure, Williams and the Rams haven't lost their belief that this can be a special season. "Man, my confidence is still as high as ever," Williams said. "We know what we've got on our team and in this locker room. We come to practice every single week. That's why we can't lose our focus. We can't lose what matters the most, and that's the work. "It's about having faith. That the work we put in every single week will come to shine." Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty will split carries with Mike Washington Jr. There's no doubt that Jeanty has been a huge disappointment for the Raiders. They picked him No. 6 overall, expecting a franchise-changing player. Instead, Jeanty has a career average of 3.5 yards per carry. And Washington has been turning heads with the coaching staff, according to a post on the Raiders' YouTube page via Athlon Sports. But he needs to be better at pass protection . "He's a rookie, so he had a lot to catch up on," Kubiak said when asked about Washington's role in the passing game. "He's continuing to improve. (And) he's putting the work in. You see the practice come to life in the games. He's not where he wants to be. He's got to keep growing." Jeanty has been a threat in the passing game. Maybe his future is as a third-down back. Washington could supplant him. And the prediction is for that to begin this week. Jeanty has time to bounce back. It's still early in his career. But he simply hasn't been able to show in the NFL what he showed in college. picks.blurb: NFL Week 7 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Chiefs upend Seahawks, Raiders scare Rams Skip to main content NFL NFL Standings NFL Free Agency NFL News by Team More NFL News Our NFL Sites MLB Standings MLB Trades and Transactions MLB Free Agency Baseball Insiders MLB News by Team More MLB News Our MLB Sites Draft Tracker NBA Free Agency NBA Standings NBA News by Team More NBA News Our NBA Sites Anaheim Ducks Boston Bruins Buffalo Sabres Calgary Flames Carolina Hurricanes Chicago Blackhawks Colorado Avalanche Columbus Blue Jackets Detroit Red Wings Edmonton Oilers Florida Panthers Los Angeles Kings Minnesota Wild Montreal Canadiens Nashville Predators New Jersey Devils New York Islanders New York Rangers Ottawa Senators Philadelphia Flyers Pittsburgh Penguins San Jose Sharks Seattle Kraken St. Louis Blues Tampa Bay Lightning Toronto Maple Leafs Vancouver Canucks Vegas Golden Knights Washington Capitals Winnipeg Jets COLLEGE College Football Men's College Basketball Women's College Basketball Men's College Baseball ABOUT Contact Meet the Editorial Team Our Entertainment Sites The Kansas City Chiefs have been as reliable as possible, the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams have not, the Las Vegas Raiders seem like they just won't go away, and it's safe to say the regular season has gotten off to a wild and weird start as we head into NFL Week 7 . Our picks and predictions each week have been indicative of that. Sorry I didn't have the Arizona Cardinals beating the Rams outright or the Tennessee Titans getting their first win of the season. We persevere and keep going with the picks. It's going to be a fun Week 7 in the league, as the NFL has big-time matchups like Cowboys-Eagles (less exciting than it once was), Chiefs-Seahawks, Rams-Raiders, Packers-Lions and even Patriots-Bears on Thursday night. That's enough to set the stage alone, so let's get right into our NFL Week 7 picks with predictions straight-up and against the spread for every game this week. NFL Week 7 predictions: Picks straight-up and ATS for every game Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFL Week 7 Matchup Straight-Up Pick Patriots vs. Bears (TNF) Steelers vs. Saints (Paris) Buccaneers vs. Panthers Panthers -3.5 49ers vs. Falcons Bengals vs. Ravens Giants vs. Texans Dolphins vs. Jets Browns vs. Titans Colts vs. Vikings Broncos vs. Cardinals Cardinals +4.5 Rams vs. Raiders Packers vs. Lions Chiefs vs. Seahawks Cowboys vs. Eagles 2026 NFL Picks Straight-Up Record: 58-35 (Last week 7-7) | ATS Record: 43-48-2 (Last week 6-8) Note: All lines are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 7 prediction to make Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Frankly, there were a lot of tough predictions to make, but taking the Chiefs to go on the road to Seattle and hand the Seahawks another loss outright feels like the one I struggled with the most. With all due respect to the 12th Man and the impact that could have on this game, there's a lot to be worried about when it comes to the Seahawks right now. Sam Darnold and this offense are in dire straits, particularly with their inability to effectively run the ball, which then puts it all on the shoulders of a quarterback who, outside of the playoffs last year, has been exceptionally turnover-prone. That then, in turn, puts way too much pressure on this defense. Then there's the Chiefs, a team that has a defense under Steve Spagnuolo that feels tailor-made to be able to put Darnold into turnover-prone positions in this game. Now, to be sure, the Kansas City passing offense hasn't been operating on all cylinders, so I do wonder what Mike Macdonald will have in store to try and bottle up Kenneth Walker III. At the end of the day, though, there's simply more I trust with the Chiefs right now than with Seahawks, so even on the road, give me KC. Easiest NFL Week 7 pick on the board New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Don't mistake this for having any type of unwavering faith in the New York Jets. It's wavering quite a bit. At the same time, maybe the thing that I'm most confident in right now is the fact that the Miami Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL. Yes, they might win a game randomly at some point this season, but I have a hard time believing that win comes on the road and that it comes against a team that is at least as healthy as the Jets are right now in this moment. The Dolphins don't have anyone that can cover Garrett Wilson or even Omar Cooper Jr. in the passing game, which should give Geno Smith some consistent options in the pass game, while Braelon Allen and the offensive line are getting the run game clicking. The defense is fine overall, but the pass rush against a team that's not without De'Von Achane leads me to believe that Malik Willis is going to have a tough time on Sunday. This feels almost too simple, but I can't pass it up. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) I know, I know, I know. My Bo Nix slander has gone entirely too far. I can hear you complaining about it now, and it's a fair point, because even after beating the Rams, I'm under no guise that the Cardinals are a high-quality football team. At the same time, though, Nix is playing like the worst quarterback in the NFL right now. Even as someone low on Nix, I didn't expect this type of dramatic dropoff with no real signs of things getting any better. The Cardinals defense is certainly a generous unit, but I don't know if Sean Payton or Nix himself have enough faith in the quarterback right now to fully take advantage of that. Moreover, the defense has, on the whole, been lesser than a year ago and has been quite banged up. While the ceiling of the Cardinals is low, I don't think that Jacoby Brissett is going to make the same back-breaking mistakes we saw Sam Darnold make on Thursday Night Football last week. This feels like a game that could end up being similarly weird to Arizona's win over the Rams this past week, and I'm not only taking the Cards against the spread in this matchup, but give me them to pull off the upset fully while playing at home. away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams are preparing to play the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7, and the injuries just keep piling up. Earlier this week , the Rams placed wide receiver Davante Adams and nose tackle Poona Ford on injured reserve. Additionally, defensive lineman Kobie Turner has been ruled out for a handful of weeks. “Trent will be a DNP with his groin. We'll take it a day at a time, like what I told you guys, and evaluate his status as we go,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Then on Monday, found out Landman landed in the concussion protocol so he'll be a DNP.” While Landman's presence on the injury report isn’t surprising given that he’s been there the last few weeks, his placement in the concussion protocol is certainly a new development. In order to return to play, Landman will be limited in his allowed activity. He’ll then graduate to an aerobic exercise program overseen by the club’s medical staff. Lastly, after leaving Kobie Turner off the injured reserve transactions on Tuesday alongside Davante Adams and Poona Ford, the Rams placed him on injured reserve Wednesday. Turner will be out for a minimum of four weeks. In corresponding moves, the Rams signed EDGE Darryl Peterson III to the active roster and signed Jalen Hunt to the practice squad. “Everybody sees these and they're on their fantasy team or whatever and they're like, 'I have to trade a guy in and out now.' We're like, 'Well, that guy has worked his ass off for the last eight months to get this opportunity and it's unfortunate he doesn't get to do what he loves to do,’” said quarterback Matthew Stafford. “I feel more for our guys than I do for anybody else.I know the work that they put into it to be out here doing what they love, so that hurts me for them. But at the same time, I think I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win.” For the Raiders, defensive lineman Tonka Hemingway was the only non-participant as he remains in the concussion protocol. The Rams will certainly monitor the statuses of tight end Brock Bowers, offensive tackle Kolton Miller, and linebacker Quay Walker. All three were limited on Wednesday. However, the Rams will be monitoring other key starters as well this week. On Wednesday, cornerback Trent McDuffie didn’t practice with a groin injury and remains day-to-day. Additionally, linebacker Nate Landman has been placed in the concussion protocol. McDuffie was a late addition to the injury report last week. While McVay said that he felt good about him going into Sunday, McDuffie was inactive for the game. McDuffie will certainly be one to monitor this week. away.headline: Rams are dealing with a new Puka Nacua injury concern
away.blurb: Rams star wide receiver Puka Nacua had to leave practice early on Thursday due to a calf injury, Sarah Barshop of ESPN reports . Barshop adds that Nacua is officially being listed as limited on the injury report as a a result. The injury bug cannot stop biting the Los Angeles Rams. The Rams are set to play the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday as part of Week 7 action. As a result, Nacua’s status for that game now appears to be in some real question. Nacua, the 25-year-old All-Pro selection, has caught 37 passes for 417 yards and just one touchdown through four games this season. That production has been hampered by a number of previous injuries, including a psoas (groin) issue that plagued him through training camp and a hip injury that caused Nacua to miss two weeks of action earlier in the year . Entering this season as a Super Bowl favorite, the Rams are off to a disappointing 2-4 start to the 2026 campaign. While they are still listed as 5.5-point favorites over the Raiders on Sunday, it looks like Los Angeles could be without their WR1 Nacua for that matchup. That continues on what has been a miserable last several weeks for the Rams from an injury standpoint. In addition to all of their injuries on the defensive side of the ball, Los Angeles is already without multiple other pass-catchers like Terrance Ferguson (who is still recovering from an ankle issue) and Davante Adams ( who just got some rotten news on his hamstring injury ). If Nacua cannot go on Sunday either, that would leave the Rams with a bare-bones unit of receivers Konata Mumpfield and Jordan Whittington plus tight ends Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee to serve as quarterback Matthew Stafford’s primary targets. away.headline: Dear God, super-team curse is so real — NFL world takes notice as another injury concern emerges for Rams star Puka Nacua
away.blurb: The defense has also taken hits, with Myles Garrett recovering from knee surgery, Poona Ford out for the season with a triceps injury, and Kobie Turner expected to miss four to six weeks with a groin strain. Linebacker Nate Landman remains in concussion protocol, while cornerback Trent McDuffie has also dealt with a groin injury. Kicker Blake Grupe is out for the season after tearing his ACL. Analyst Holden Cantor also appeared frustrated, writing, “I’m out man.” If Nacua is unavailable against the Raiders, receiver Konata Mumpfield could be asked to take on a bigger role. The Rams face an urgent must-win scenario against Las Vegas to prevent their season from spiraling out of reach, but this spate of injuries could test Sean McVay’s resolve. The Los Angeles Rams’ season is turning into a growing injury nightmare, and Puka Nacua could be the latest star to miss some time. The wide receiver left Thursday’s practice early with a calf injury, putting his availability for Sunday’s Week 7 clash against the Las Vegas Raiders in doubt. Los Angeles entered the 2026 season with Super Bowl hopes, but a growing list of injuries has made that goal harder to reach. Their recent 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals dropped them to 2-4 and the bottom of the NFC West. Now, Nacua’s injury has given fans and analysts another reason to worry as the team looks to get its season back on track. NFL World Reacts to Puka Nacua’s Injury Nacua’s injury has added to the frustration surrounding a Rams team already missing several key players. Wide receiver Davante Adams is on Injured Reserve with a severe hamstring injury, while tight end Terrance Ferguson remains sidelined with an ankle issue. The growing injury list has prompted strong reactions from fans and analysts. ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky summed up his reaction in two words, writing, “Dear God.” The Sleeper News channel also expressed frustration, posting , “Not Puka man.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Analyst Field Yates shared a similar reaction, writing, “Ah crap.” One fan pointed to the number of injuries affecting the team, saying, “‘Super Team’ curse so real in the NFL.” Meanwhile, analyst Derek Brown questioned the Rams’ offseason draft decisions in light of their current problems. “I feel like MAYBE the Rams should have drafted a WR this year instead of a QB & a TE,” Brown wrote. Puka Nacua Has Been a Key Target for Matthew Stafford Despite missing time earlier in the season with a groin/hip issue, Nacua has been Matthew Stafford’s most reliable receiving option when healthy. In four games, the wide receiver has recorded 37 receptions for 417 yards and one touchdown. He has an 81.8 PFN WR Impact Grade , which ranks 15th among wide receivers. home.headline: Mike Washington Jr. misses Las Vegas Raiders’ Thursday practice ahead of Week 7 Los Angeles Rams’ matchup
home.blurb: Washington was listed as a limited participant with foot and back injuries during Wednesday's session, but was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's injury report. So, it appears he suffered a setback. The fourth-round pick has been the second back behind Ashton Jeanty through the first six games this season but had 10 touches for 50 yards from scrimmage last week against the Buffalo Bills, including nine rushes for 43 yards . His role is expected to increase as the Silver and Black figure out their rushing woes, ranking 30th in the NFL for total rushing yards and 31st in yards per attempt this fall. Obviously, that requires Washington to be healthy, though. Meanwhile, Jeanty, who has also battled injuries this year, hasn't been listed on the injury report this week and appears to be a full go. So, if Washington isn't available, the offense will still have its lead back, barring a significant change in the coming days. In other injury news, defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway was spotted wearing a red, non-contact jersey on Thursday, per Warren . Hemingway suffered a concussion against the New England Patriots two weeks ago and missed last Sunday's game against the Buffalo Bills. Wearing the red jersey suggests he's limited in practice and one step closer to clearing the NFL's concussion protocol. Warren also posted a video of tight end Brock Bowers warming up before Thursday's practice. Bowers was limited Wednesday with hamstring and calf injuries, which is different from the knee injury that caused him to miss Weeks 1 and 2. That being said, he's been limited on Wednesdays every week since returning to action. The Raiders released the official injury report, in which Bowers (hamstring/calf), defensive tackle Foley Fatukasi (shoulder) and offensive tackle Kolton Miller (shoulder) were upgraded from limited to full participants during the team's second practice of the week. Additionally, Hemingway was confirmed to be limited. home.headline: Raiders TE Brock Bowers gets eye-opening upgrade on injury report before Rams game
home.blurb: Bowers was limited on Wednesday because of hamstring and calf injuries . He missed the first two games of the 2026 season after undergoing a minor knee procedure shortly before the campaign began. His latest injury report designation is the first time this season he has been listed with an issue other than his knee. Bowers' return to full practice participation comes as the Raiders attempt to end a three-game losing streak. Over their past three games, Las Vegas has been outscored 64-41 after halftime, including a 24-3 disadvantage in the third quarter. The Raiders have also committed seven second-half turnovers this season, with four of quarterback Kirk Cousins' five interceptions occurring during the final two quarters. Las Vegas has shown offensive potential, averaging 26.7 points per game, the sixth-highest mark in the league. However, inconsistent red-zone execution and defensive woes have prevented the Raiders from consistently closing out games. Alongside Bowers, defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi and offensive tackle Kolton Miller also returned to full participation after being limited Wednesday. Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway was limited after missing the previous practice, while running back Mike Washington did not participate and linebacker Quay Walker remained limited. Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway was the only non-participant for the Raiders. Five other players were limited, including Brock Bowers and Kolton Miller. Both of these teams have playoff expectations in 2026, but they’re in very different spots through six weeks of the season. Seattle is coming off a bad loss to Denver on Thursday Night Football in Week 6, as Sam Darnold threw multiple picks and the Seattle offense struggled to get anything going against an elite Denver defense. That dropped the Seahawks to 3-3, and they’re multiple games out of first place in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Kansas City defense put on a clinic in Week 6, holding the Los Angeles Chargers to just six points to move to 5-0 in the 2026 season. There is a huge revenge game possibly on Sunday, as Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III returns to Seattle for the first time since he won Super Bowl MVP for the ‘Hawks. The Seahawks let the star back go in free agency, and he’s been a monster for the Chiefs this season, rushing for 665 yards and six scores in just five games. Even though the Chiefs have a better record, Seattle is favored at home in this marquee matchup. Let’s take a look at the opening odds and some things to watch for in primetime in Week 7. There is clearly some confidence in this Seattle defense with an extended rest at home against Kansas City. The Chiefs have not lost this season, but they are banged up at the receiver position with Rashee Rice missing Week 6 and Tyquan Thornton on injured reserve. Oddsmakers seem to think this is a spot where the Chiefs will lose their first game in 2026. Chiefs vs. Seahawks Betting Preview These are two of the best defenses in the league, which isn’t what you’d usually think about when referring to a Patrick Mahomes-led squad. The Chiefs traded away Trent McDuffie in the offseason, yet they’re third in the league in EPA/Play and success rate and fourth in EPA/Pass. That could be an issue for a Seattle team that is heavily reliant on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, especially since Sam Darnold has thrown seven interceptions already this season. Seattle (No. 2 in EPA/Play on defense) completely shut down Bo Nix and the Broncos in Week 6, but it wasn’t enough with this offense still struggling. Seattle is just 25th in EPA/Play and 20th in success rate on that side of the ball through six games. It makes sense that the defending champs are favored at home, but there is one stat that I can’t look past when it comes to Mahomes. He’s been a road underdog 12 times in his career, going 10-1-1 against the spread and 9-3 straight up. The Chiefs look like one of the best teams in the NFL, and I expect that to remain the case in Week 7. I don’t mind getting 2.5 points with them as an early lean for this primetime matchup. picks.headline: Seahawks Get Devastating News on Former 2nd-Round Pick Before Chiefs Game
picks.blurb: Seahawks Get Devastating News on Former 2nd-Round Pick Before Chiefs Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview Seahawks Get Devastating News on Former 2nd-Round Pick Before Chiefs Game SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 30: Elijah Arroyo #18 of the Seattle Seahawks reacts to a play in the third quarter of a game against the Minnesota Vikings at Lumen Field on November 30, 2025 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jane Gershovich/Getty Images) Getty Duncan Day Thu, October 22, 2026 at 9:08 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Elijah Arroyo #18 of the Seattle Seahawks is assisted off the field after a play against the Denver Broncos during the second quarter of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) Getty SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 11: AJ Barner #88 of the Seattle Seahawks catches the ball against the San Francisco 49ers at Lumen Field on October 17, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty The Seattle Seahawks have suffered a season-ending injury blow to one of their promising young offensive weapons. Second-year tight end Elijah Arroyo is undergoing shoulder surgery Thursday, Oct. 22, and will miss the remainder of the 2026 season. ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter reported the development Thursday, delivering a disappointing verdict on Seattle's former second-round draft pick. "Source: Seahawks TE Elijah Arroyo is undergoing shoulder surgery today and will miss the rest of the season," Schefter wrote. The announcement comes just three days before Seattle hosts the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs in a highly anticipated Sunday Night Football matchup. It also marks a significant reversal from earlier expectations that Arroyo might return following a relatively brief absence. Seahawks Lose Arroyo for Rest of 2026 Season GettyDENVER, COLORADO – OCTOBER 15: Elijah Arroyo #18 of the Seattle Seahawks is assisted off the field after a play against the Denver Broncos during the second quarter of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) Arroyo suffered the shoulder injury during Seattle's 17-14 loss to the Denver Broncos on October 15. The 23-year-old exited during the second quarter and was initially listed as doubtful to return. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald revealed the following day that Arroyo was undergoing further examination to determine the severity of the injury. "He's getting some imaging and testing as we speak, so no update yet," Macdonald said, per the team's official website . ESPN's Jeremy Fowler subsequently reported October 19 that Arroyo was likely headed to injured reserve, which would require him to miss at least four games. That outlook has now changed dramatically. Rather than potentially returning for Seattle's late-season push, Arroyo will spend the remainder of the campaign recovering from surgery. The setback is particularly frustrating considering his draft pedigree. Seattle selected the former Miami standout with the No. 50 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft following a breakout collegiate season in which he recorded 35 receptions, 590 yards and seven touchdowns. Arroyo flashed potential as a rookie, catching 15 passes for 179 yards and one touchdown across 13 regular-season appearances. A knee injury interrupted his debut campaign and sidelined him for the final four regular-season games, although he eventually returned for Seattle's championship-winning postseason run. His second season offered an opportunity to build on that foundation. Instead, Arroyo managed just one reception for 17 yards in 2026 before his latest injury brought the season to a premature conclusion. Seahawks Have Tight End Decision Following Arroyo Injury GettySEATTLE, WASHINGTON – OCTOBER 11: AJ Barner #88 of the Seattle Seahawks catches the ball against the San Francisco 49ers at Lumen Field on October 17, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Arroyo's absence leaves Seattle without a young pass-catching option who was expected to develop into a larger contributor. Fortunately for the Seahawks, AJ Barner remains established as the team's starting tight end. Barner has recorded 15 receptions for 138 yards through six games this season. He finished 2025 with 52 catches, 519 yards and six touchdowns. Veteran Eric Saubert and Nick Kallerup also provide depth at the position. Seattle had already taken steps to reinforce the group before Schefter's announcement. On Monday, Oct. 19, the Seahawks signed veteran tight end Josiah Deguara to their practice squad. Deguara, a former third-round selection by the Green Bay Packers , has appeared in 78 NFL games with 12 starts. He has accumulated 53 receptions for 471 yards and three touchdowns during his career. Whether Seattle makes another move following Arroyo's season-ending diagnosis remains to be seen. For now, the immediate challenge is preparing for Kansas City without the young tight end. The Seahawks enter Sunday's matchup at 3-3 following consecutive losses to Denver and the San Francisco 49ers . With Arroyo unavailable, Seattle will have to lean on its remaining tight ends as the team attempts to reverse that slide and regain ground in the NFC West. picks.blurb: The dynamic running back broke free of his platoon in Washington state after being deemed expendable despite the Seahawks' $700 million in contract extensions to keep its core intact. That made him the balm in a terribly burned Kansas City Chiefs backfield, where he's put up an Offensive Player of the Year pace across the team's 5-0 start. Now he faces his former team in his former home in primetime. That game has us torn in Week 7. It's not the only one. Welcome back to For The Win's straight-up, moneyline NFL picks column. I ended 2023 as Pickwatch’s top expert in a field of hundreds. The two seasons that followed? Ehhhhh, we don't like to talk about that. But I'm back and hopeful I'll either be good enough to rejoin the top 25 or, barring that, be so destructively bad you're left with no choice but to fade my picks all the way to prosperity. Joining me for 2026 is a six-person panel ranging from FTW editors (Charles Curtis, Wajih AlBaroudi and Jeff Smith) to betting analysts (Prince Grimes) to NFL writers (Robert Zeglinski and Andrew Joseph). Here are our Week 7 picks. Patriots at Bears Steelers at Saints Bengals at Ravens Browns at Titans Colts at Vikings Dolphins at Jets Giants at Texans 49ers at Falcons Bucs at Panthers Broncos at Cardinals Packers at Lions Rams at Raiders Chiefs at Seahawks Cowboys at Eagles Season to date: Since our editing software occasionally struggles to make these picks super clear, here they are in an easier to read (but impossible to cut and paste) .jpg you can click to expand: Let's break out three games to talk about. Survivor pick of the week: New York Jets (-4.5) over the Miami Dolphins Cool, I've murdered you once again. While I appreciate some Indianapolis Colts schadenfreude, I'm truly not enjoying this year's survivor slate. Ah well, time to back another flawed team with a quarterback working through yet another redemption arc. The Dolphins are coming off a bye and scored 24 points their last time out, but that was also the only week this season in which they've topped 13. New York's defense is competent. The Jets offense just got a boost with Omar Cooper Jr. returning to the lineup. Geno Smith faces the league's second-worst passing defense. If he can't thrive here, it's time to fade back into "high value backup" status. Last week : 1-0 Season to date : 3-3 Hardest favorite to back: Baltimore Ravens (-1.5) over the Cincinnati Bengals Oh, friends, do I ever hate this pick. We're writing this on Wednesday and don't know what Lamar Jackson has planned for the week. If he's playing? I'm in. If not? This flips to Joe Shiesty and company. But, for now, let's assume we get an 80 percent Jackson behind center. Why I like this pick : The AFC North isn't defined by logic and answers only to the gods of chaos and violence. Baltimore has fielded the slightly better defense, and an emerging Ja'Kobi Lane brings an important fallback option. The Ravens find an extra gear against Cincinnati, beating the Bengals five of their last six tries and scoring at least 24 points in each of those wins. Why I don't like this pick : Even if Jackson plays, he'll have to face a revitalized and suddenly viable Bengals pass rush that has a strategy beyond "throw Trey Hendrickson at them, hope it works." away.headline: Chiefs provide update on Josh Simmons. Here's why he won't be back anytime soon
away.source: The Kansas City Star on MSN
away.blurb: “Josh worked his tail off,” Chiefs trainer Rick Burkholder said. “He worked diligently with my staff every day and has improved to point where he could return to practice in a limited capacity last week. “However, we feel like he’s plateaued in the rehab process as he’s trying to get to the final steps of recovery with the return to competition. He’s just not there yet. Burkholder said Simmons missed Wednesday’s practice to discuss the developments, and that’s why he was listed on the injury report as being out with a back injury and for personal reasons. “It was decided and agreed upon by everybody - his people, his agent, him, myself, (Chiefs head coach) Andy (Reid), (general manager Brett) Veach - that he should be placed on IR to give him more time to return to full function.” Josh Simmons’ rehabilitation has “plateaued,” and he’s been placed in the injured reserve list. The Chiefs shared the news about their second-year left tackle on Thursday. “After discussion with Josh (Wednesday), we gave him some time to talk with his family and his representatives to investigate next steps as he goes through this process.” That means Simmons will miss at least the next four games. Simmons, the Chiefs’ first-round draft pick in 2025, experienced a bulging, herniated disk in training camp and hasn’t appeared in a game yet this season. Undrafted free agent Khalil Benson has stepped in to Simmons’ role. The Chiefs could be without their other starting tackle, Jaylon Moore, for Sunday night’s game at the Seattle Seahawks. Moore suffered a concussion in last week’s game against the LA Chargers. Joshua Ezeude finished the game at right tackle.

away.headline: Fans fear for Josh Simmons' career as Chiefs star is ruled out again
away.blurb: He is currently dealing with a bulging disk in his lower back and will be out at least four more weeks - having already missed the first five games of the season. Last October, Simmons was involved in a bizarre and mysterious saga after he missed Kansas City's win over the Detroit Lions . Just hours before kickoff, he was listed as 'questionable' for 'personal' reasons before being downgraded to out. 'Josh worked his tail off. He worked diligently with my staff every day, and he improved to the point where he returned to practice in a limited capacity last week,' Burkholder said. MORE: Fury as winless Miami Dolphins announce they will hike ticket prices Josh Simmons' NFL future was plunged into more doubt on Thursday after the former first round pick was placed on injured reserve. Simmons was selected by Kansas City with the 32nd overall pick of the 2025 draft. It was hoped he would become their franchise left tackle. But the 23-year-old has started just eight games in a difficult start to his NFL career as injuries and personal matters have kept him off the field. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes later said he was surprised by Simmons' absence, with reports claiming coaches 'didn't know' where he was. Head coach Andy Reid was reluctant to discuss his absence but did say Simmons was 'taking care of family'. The left tackle later said he wanted to keep precise details 'in house.' He missed four games before eventually returning to the field in mid-November. Three games later, however, a fractured and dislocated hand landed him on IR for the remainder of the season. The 23-year-old showed up to training camp in late July hoping his injury issues were behind him. But on August 17, he reported feeling some discomfort in his calf, and the Chiefs' training staff determined it was stemming from his back. Chiefs trainer Rick Burkholder obtained an MRI exam that confirmed the herniated and bulging disk, which was 'higher up than we normally see in our offensive linemen, which complicated the case.' The Chiefs recommended a second opinion, and a back specialist in California believed that Simmons would be able to overcome the injury with rehabilitation rather than surgery. That is why the Chiefs had not put Simmons on injured reserve until Thursday. 'However we feel he plateaued in the recovery process... he's just not there yet.' After discussing the situation with Simmons, his family and representatives, the decision was made to place him on IR. 'It was decided and agreed upon by everybody,' Burkholder said, adding that surgery still is not in the forecast. It means undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson will continue to protect the blind side of quarterback Mahomes, starting with Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks.

home.blurb: Look, this injury hurts because Elijah Arroyo was just starting to carve out a role. The Seahawks took him in the second round of the 2025 NFL draft with the 50th overall pick. That's real draft capital for a tight end. He tore his ACL in September of 2022 at Miami. That injury limited him to only nine games across the 2022 and 2023 seasons. He bounced back and put together a great college career with the Hurricanes, which is a big reason Seattle used a second-round pick on him. Arroyo got hurt in last Thursday night's primetime loss to the Denver Broncos as he was trying to recover a fumble by wide receiver Rashid Shaheed. It's a brutal way to lose a season, and it's even tougher for a second-year player who still has a lot to prove. The numbers tell the story. Arroyo will miss 11 games for Seattle, plus any potential postseason run. Seahawks fans won't see him on the field again until 2027. home.blurb: Charbonnet, who sustained a torn ACL that required surgery in a divisional-round playoff victory last season, was a full participant in practice Wednesday and might be able to return this weekend. Seattle's ground game has struggled without Charbonnet and first-round pick Jadarian Price (chest/shoulder), who has been on injured reserve since Week 2. Fellow linebacker Tyrice Knight (oblique) and wide receiver Rashid Shaheed (hip) were among the players who were limited. The NFL's top rusher will lead his new team, the Kansas City Chiefs (5-0), into a primetime matchup Sunday against the defending NFL champion Seahawks (3-3), for whom he won the Super Bowl MVP award last season. "I'm just focused on critiquing the mistakes we made," said Walker, referring to last weekend's sluggish 22-6 victory against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. "Once we get to that point (Seattle), we'll see." For the soft-spoken Walker, that wasn't surprising. But others, on both teams, had plenty to say. "I know it's going to be a special moment for him to get back to the place where you kind of built your career and won a Super Bowl," Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes said. " ... But at the end of the day, we have to win a football game." Seahawks safety Julian Love said it's been "weird for sure" watching film of Walker break off long runs for the Chiefs. "He's doing what he did for us last season, the past bunch of seasons for the Seahawks. And he's picked up where he left off from last season," Love said. "His tape looks incredible. Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (knee) was a limited participant in practice again. His time on the field is regularly managed due to a lingering knee issue. The Chiefs seemingly opened a roster spot for McDonald by waiving linebacker Cam Jones on Tuesday. Veteran defensive end Demarcus Lawrence (non-injury related - rest) was a limited participant in practice on Thursday after sitting out on Wednesday. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens (-3) Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . It was their 15th loss when leading by at least seven points in the fourth quarter since 2020, which ranks the most in the NFL. Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this week, but I'm curious to see how "spry" he looks. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27 Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. If he's not, then you can switch my pick to the Bengals. If Jackson is in alongside Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers , I just don't think this Baltimore offense can be stopped. When those three have shared the field this season, the Ravens are averaging 9.9 yards per play. NINE POINT NINE. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. If there is any team that can compete with an explosive offense, it's probably the Bengals, but I don't see them quite keeping up here. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bengals 26 Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani ( Lions -3): Just take the Over in this matchup. The Lions really burned me coming off the bye last year, losing to J.J. McCarthy , but I'm going to back them in this spot. The concern is, of course, the defense, which ranks dead last in the NFL with 404.4 total yards surrendered per game. HOWEVER, I will mention that Kelvin Sheppard 's unit forced five straight three-and-outs from the Cardinals in that 45-21 win in Week 5. Plus, Brian Branch is set to return to the lineup as well. Give me the Lions at home. … Prediction: Lions 35, Packers 30 Dubin (Lions -3): This one has all the makings of a shootout, with two explosive offenses going back and forth. Jared Goff and Co. are coming off the bye, and they have scored 31 or more points in four of their five games to date — and they scored 26 while piling up 452 yards in the other one. Nobody except maybe Kenneth Walker III is doing it at a higher level than Jahmyr Gibbs right now, either. Meanwhile, Green Bay can throw the ball all over the yard, and everyone throws it on the Lions. Maybe Green Bay can actually run with some efficiency in Josh Jacobs ' potential return, but it's not like he was all that efficient last season, either. I lean toward the Lions because they can beat you both ways. … Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 28 Kansas City Chiefs at Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) (SNF) Dajani (Chiefs +2.5): The Seahawks looked completely disinterested in that Week 6 loss to the Denver Broncos . Dallas is off to a slow start at 2-4, and the defense (31st in EPA/Play) remains one of the worst in the NFL. Dak Prescott and Co. have lost back-to-back primetime games against Tampa Bay (Week 5) and Green Bay (Week 6), looking pretty rough in both appearances. So, can they turn things around on the road against a divisional opponent? The Eagles enter this game on a four-game losing streak, and star quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots in his lungs. That is a massive blow to the Eagles in the futures market, as they’re now last in the odds to win the NFC East and +15000 to win the Super Bowl. Tanner McKee is set to make another start in Week 7, and this may turn into a lost season for an Eagles team that could decide to trade some veteran pieces to recoup draft capital and lighten the load on the salary cap in years to come. Oddsmakers have set the Cowboys as favorites in this matchup, and a win would put Dallas in a much better position to win the NFC East – which it is still favored to do. Plus, the Cowboys’ offense looked awful on Sunday night in a loss to Green Bay, which may have caused the move in this line on Monday morning. Cowboys vs. Eagles Betting Preview The Eagles have covered the spread just once in the 2026 season (in their London loss to Jacksonville), so it’s hard to justify betting on them with a backup at quarterback. If Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is able to return in Week 7, it could flip these odds even further towards the Eagles. Dallas needs to figure things out on offense, as Prescott has struggled with turnovers (not all his fault) in the last few games while the offensive line allowed him to take a ton of big hits in Week 6. A win for Philly could bump it back up into at least the No. 3 spot in the odds to win the NFC East, but it seems pretty clear that oddsmakers expect Dallas to eventually figure things out and advance as the division winner. Bettors may want to consider the OVER (44.5) with how poor the Dallas defense has been this season. The OVER is 4-2 in Dallas’ six games and 3-3 in the Eagles’ matchup in 2026. picks.headline: Eagles vs. Cowboys prediction as Philadelphia adjusts without Jalen Hurts
picks.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys were figured to be the two frontrunners in the NFC East this season, with some even considering the duo as Super Bowl contenders. Just six weeks into the season, both teams are closer to booking vacations than they are preparing for a February trip to Los Angeles. Injuries did a number on the Eagles, claiming Saquon Barkley and many more. Recently, Jalen Hurts was added to that list. The quarterback is done for the year with blood clots . As for Dallas, it's still the defense. And it always has been. In recent weeks, though, the Cowboys offense has become a major problem as well. That isn't a winning combination for Brian Schottenheimer, who has seen his job security come into question lately. Both teams are desperate for a win, but at least the Eagles have a built-in excuse. Dallas will try to right the ship, but can they do it in a hostile Philadelphia environment? Eagles vs Cowboys odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Eagles -3 Moneyline: Eagles -162; Cowboys +136 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Eagles Keys To Victory Stay in the fight. For all intents and purposes, the Eagles season is over after it was revealed Jalen Hurts would miss the remainder of the campaign with blood clots. Injuries have mounted, but there is still talent on this Philadelphia roster. And with the way Dallas is playing, the Eagles just have to stick around long enough to let the Cowboys beat themselves. That leaky defense and anemic offense will give the home team plenty of opportunities to win. The Eagles just have to take them. Cowboys Keys To Victory Show up. On paper, Dallas should run away with this game against an offense that can't possibly keep up. However, the Cowboys looked disinterested in Week 6 and have looked that way for quite some time. This is the perfect get-right spot against a division rival. If the Cowboys don't beat themselves, they'll win the game. Injuries to watch • RB Saquon Barkley • OL Landon Dickerson • DL Jordan Davis • LB Nolan Smith • LB Jaylx Hunt • WR KaVontae Turpin • LB DeMarvion Overshown • LB Dee Winters Eagles vs Cowboys USA TODAY expert picks Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Eagles 23, Cowboys 17 The Eagles are injured. The Cowboys are lifeless. One of them has to win. How's that for a promo? Dallas is clearly the more talented team on paper, but something stinks about this group, and it's hard to pinpoint where the smell is coming from. The defense isn't competitive. The offense appears to be going through the motions. After a rough week for the Eagles, they should be motivated to stop the bleeding and get back in the win column. And what better way to do that than against a hated rival? Even if it's only for a moment, the home team finally gives the fans a reason to smile. Adam Kaufman: Cowboys 24, Eagles 20 Not sure how many times I'm going to put myself in position to be let down by the Cowboys this season, but here we are again. With Jalen Hurts out for the season, the Eagles need Tanner McKee to stabilize an offense that was already having problems. Dallas' vulnerable defense – to put it kindly – gives him an opportunity, especially if Philadelphia can establish the run. On the other side, Dak Prescott's offense has been largely absent each of the last two weeks. But the superior talent undeniably belongs to the Cowboys and, if they can protect the ball, I like them to bounce back in a pivotal division matchup. away.headline: Dallas Cowboys Injury Updates After Week 6 Loss Include Another Starting Defender
away.blurb: Dee Winters suffered what was labeled an ankle injury in the first half of the Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers and the veteran wasn't able to return after that. It figures that Winters would get hurt during a game in which he made an impact play with an interception he nearly returned for a touchdown. Winters wasn't the only notable player to get hurt, as wideout and returner KaVontae Turpin came down with a ribs injury on the opening kickoff and did not return, either. The Cowboys replaced Turpin with wide receiver Jonathan Mingo on punt returns and running back Tyler Goodson on kickoffs. The former averaged six yards per return and had a long of 16 yards and the latter broke off a 30-yard return and averaged 24.4 pre return over five attempts. Putting that aside for now, Overshown finally returned to practice last week and turned in two limited sessions in total, so it appears he's at least getting closer to returning. That said, we have expected Overshown back for a few weeks now, yet the veteran is still out, so nobody should get their hopes up for Overshown returning to the field this week. away.headline: Cowboys vs. Eagles Injury Report
away.blurb: "It felt good to be back out there on the field with the guys practicing," Barkley told reporters. Part of Barkley's frustration is that he's never dealt with a hamstring injury before. He's sought out plenty of advice on how to manage it. "You want to be out there and try to help the team," Barkley said. "Hopefully I'll be able to go Monday." "Your play-action pass game gets better and better as you run the football better," Head Coach Nick Sirianni said. "We know we have to play not only complementary football offensively, defensively, special teams, but also within the offense. For your play-action game to create the plays that you want it to create, your run game's got to be going. You've got to be converting on third downs. You've got to be in manageable situations to continue to get reps and plays out there. away.headline: Breaking down Packers' final injury report of Week 6 vs. Cowboys
away.blurb: LG Aaron Banks (toe/knee): He practiced in a limited capacity all week, but it's his first week back from a multi-week injury. More than likely, the Packers will go with Laken Tomlinson at left guard against the Cowboys. Eventually, the Packers will have to make a long-term decision on their preferred starter at the position. DL Anthony Campbell (ankle) : His likely return from an ankle injury is coming at a good time considering the injury situation along the defensive front. It's possible Campbell will need to play double-digit snaps behind Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks and Chris McClellan on Sunday night. CB Brandon Cisse (hip): An unexpected addition to the injury report. Cisse injured his hip and was limited on Friday, creating the dreaded late-week injury and potential need to scramble for answers at a key position. Carrington Valentine would likely start if Cisse can't go. Depth at cornerback is under real stress ahead of matchup with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. WR Savion Williams (ankle): Is the second-year receiver ready to return from an ankle injury that had him on injured reserve to start the season? A natural replacement option for Skyy Moore, who is out, Williams could provide help as a gadget weapon on offense and in the return game if the Packers activate him to the 53-man roster before Sunday night. WR/KR Skyy Moore (ankle): The Packers' primary kick and punt returner injured his ankle last week and wasn't able to practice this week. It's possible the Packers will activate Savion Williams to help make up for Moore's absence in the return game and at receiver. The Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant and rookie offensive lineman Drew Shelton and listed linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, defensive lineman L.T Overton, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. and cornerback Ameer Speed as questionable on the final injury report. Receiver CeeDee Lamb (thigh) does not have an status designation and will play. How will the injury situation affect Sunday night's showdown with the Cowboys? Here’s an in-depth breakdown of the Packers ’ final injury report ahead of Week 6: OL Jacob Monk (quad): He's no longer a starting option at right guard, where Travis Glover or Kevin Zeitler will start Sunday, but Monk could be a backup at center and get snaps on special teams protection units if he's healthy. DL Jordon Riley (Achilles): He only just returned to practice this week, and even though the Packers need help along the defensive line, Riley is unlikely to play Sunday. He could be a factor as a run stuffer come next week or Week 8. DL Jonathan Ford (calf): His injury, combined with the season-ending injury to Javon Hargrave, puts the Packers in a tough place along the defensive front. Ford likely would have played a lot of snaps on Sunday if healthy.
